This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) and controls (n=21), meeting I3, I4 and the sample-size criterion I5. However, the VBM analyses reported are correlational (gray-matter correlations with conjunction-search accuracy) across the pooled sample and an ANOVA on extracted voxel values; the paper does not present a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast (bvFTD vs. controls) reported in MNI/Talairach space or coordinate tables that unambiguously reflect bvFTD-specific, group-level voxelwise results. Therefore it fails I6 and I7 (no clearly reported whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD to controls). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study is excluded.

This is a single-family case series with one symptomatic bvFTD proband and some healthy mutation carriers. Imaging includes FDG-PET (so I3 met) and the proband is clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4 met). However, the study does not meet required sample size (fewer than 6 bvFTD patients; I5 not met), has no control group and reports no between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met), and provides no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from a target bvFTD sample (I7 not met). Therefore it fails multiple mandatory inclusion criteria and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This study uses structural volumetric MRI with FreeSurfer ROI analyses, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts comparing bvFTD to healthy controls. Inclusion met: I4 (bvFTD patients included; bvFTD n=26) and I5 (patient group size ≥6). Inclusion not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI/volumetric analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper does not meet required imaging and whole-brain contrast criteria for inclusion.

This study is an ROI manual volumetry study of the putamen using structural T1 MRI, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise results or coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Inclusion met: I4 (contains clinically diagnosed FTD subgroup likely corresponding to bvFTD) and I5 (patient and control groups exceed n>=6). Inclusion not met: I3 (imaging modality requirement), I6 (reporting between-group contrasts in standard coordinate space), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise result). Exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) therefore applies. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a subgroup (ALS-FTD) who met criteria for bvFTD and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM (SPM/DARTEL) and TBSS results comparing that subgroup to controls; however the patient sample comprises individuals with ALS (a concurrent neurological disorder). This violates exclusion criterion E7 (samples with other neurological symptoms). Therefore the study must be excluded despite meeting the imaging and reporting criteria.

This is a single-case report (n=1) and does not meet several required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Specifically, only I3 is satisfied (FDG-PET used). The study does not meet I4 (the sample is a single patient described as 'FTLD-like' rather than a clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease group), I5 (fewer than 6 participants in the patient group), I6 (no between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to controls), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used FDG-PET and includes an FTD patient group (n=13) and controls (n=26) with voxelwise, whole-brain (Talairach) group contrasts; however, it does not specify that the FTD cases are behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Inclusion criterion I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease) is not met, and therefore criterion I6 (between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls) cannot be satisfied. All other applicable inclusion criteria were met (I3, I5, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on lack of specification of bvFTD/Pick diagnosis in the sample, so patient group does not meet the target diagnostic inclusion required by the review.

The study is excluded because it uses structural MRI morphometry (manual/automated segmentation and radial distance shape mapping of the putamen), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and reports ROI-based shape/volume analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise results with stereotactic coordinates. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD patients), I5 (sample sizes: FTD n=33, controls n=17). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural morphometry, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach coordinate space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete for assessment.

Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients among its sample (I4), has adequate sample sizes (42 patients, 30 controls; I5), and reports whole-brain VBM results for pathologic groups (so reporting format is acceptable, I8), it does NOT report a between-group contrast that directly compares a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls (in MNI/Talairach space) where the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I6). Likewise, it does not provide a whole-brain group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample (I7). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet I6 and I7.

This study examines frontal-variant FTLD (fv-FTLD), equivalent to behavioral variant FTD, using 18FDG-PET (and [11C]MDL PET) with voxelwise SPM analyses. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (sb: whole fv-FTLD vs controls; apathetic vs controls; disinhibited vs controls; direct between-group contrasts) with coordinates in MNI space and cluster-level information. Patient group (n=18) and control group (n=24) meet sample-size thresholds; PET subgroup analyses included 8 patients and 6 controls (>=6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no comorbid psychiatric/other dementia in sample, empirical FDG-PET whole-brain results reported). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study used structural MRI with VBM-based preprocessing (I3 satisfied) and included an FTD patient group (n≈12) and healthy controls (n=18) meeting minimum sample sizes (I5 satisfied). However, it does not specify behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease specifically (I4 not met). Critically, the paper reports SVM-based multivariate classification results rather than mass-univariate, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls; no group-level voxelwise results identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample are provided (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria required for this review. No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered.

This is an open-label FDG-PET study in FTD that includes a bvFTD subgroup (n=7) and reports voxelwise, group-level PET results (before vs after memantine) with coordinates. However, it does not include any between-group contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. The meta-analysis requires at least one between-group contrast of bvFTD versus controls (I6). Therefore the study fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded.

This is a longitudinal, empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (SPM2 optimized/modulated VBM) to compare MSTD (Tau +3 intron 10 mutation) patients to age- and gender-matched controls. The VBM analysis included 7 early-stage MSTD patients (all clinically diagnosed with bvFTD) and 19 controls, meeting the sample-size requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with significant clusters and refers to stereotactic locations in supplementary Table 4 (i.e., coordinates in a defined stereotactic space). Whole-brain voxelwise results are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD-target sample. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, review/meta-analysis, methods-only, or disallowed imaging modalities) are met.

This study does not meet the review’s target-sample and whole-brain contrast requirements. It includes FTLD patients (N=31) and uses 18F-FDG PET (I3 satisfied) and has sufficient patient sample size (I5 satisfied). However, it does not specify that the FTLD sample is clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not met: FTLD is reported generally without bvFTD/Pick’s subgroup breakdown). The paper also does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast in stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met) and therefore provides no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and several are not, the study must be excluded.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 — the study reports lobar/ROI volumetry (temporal and frontal lobe volumes and ratios) and does not present whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables. 
(b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 — uses automated voxel-based volumetry (SPM5-based voxel approach akin to VBM); I4 — includes a bvFTLD subgroup (6 bvFTLD patients); I5 — sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTLD n=6; controls n=30). 
(c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 — no report of at least one between-group voxelwise contrast in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTLD group to controls unpooled; I7 — no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result clearly identified for the target group. 
Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion). Therefore the study is excluded because it provides only ROI/lobar volumetry without whole-brain voxelwise contrasts required by the review.

This is an empirical VBM study of bvFTD cases (both C9ORF72 carriers and sporadic bvFTD) including healthy controls. It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (patient groups vs Controls) using MNI space and provides coordinates/figures (including supplementary table). Sample sizes meet the minimum (C9 n=8, sporadic bvFTD n=15, Controls n=15). Whole-brain group-level results for the target bvFTD groups are clearly identified. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and imaging details; therefore judged complete.

Although this study uses whole-brain VBM in MNI space and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) with adequate control numbers, the provided full text does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in standard space. It does report within-group whole-brain VBM covariate results for bvFTD (VBM correlations with IGT scores) but no explicit bvFTD vs. control voxelwise contrast coordinates/results are presented in the supplied text. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I7, I8. No exclusion criteria were triggered.

While this study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD patients (equivalent to bvFTD; I4), has sufficient patient sample size (n=70; I5), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise component images in MNI space (I7, acceptable reporting format I8), it does not present a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD/fv-FTD group directly to healthy controls in MNI or Talairach space (criterion I6). The paper focuses on within-group PCA decomposition of patient scans rather than reporting a between-group coordinate-based contrast vs controls; therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study used VBM and resting-state fMRI (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (7 bvFTD cases within the FTD-GRN+ group) (I4). Sample sizes meet minimums (14 patients, control groups ≥6) (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group results (VBM and functional maps) (I7) and presents results in figures/tables (I8). However, the critical requirement I6 is not met: the reported between-group contrasts compare a combined FTD-GRN+ group (mixing bvFTD and avPPA) to controls rather than reporting a bvFTD-only versus control whole-brain contrast. The bvFTD subgroup is pooled with other FTD phenotypes in the main analyses, so no bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrast is available. No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing inclusion criterion I6.

This study used Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (satisfies I3) and includes sufficient participant numbers across patient and control groups (satisfies I5). However, it does not report results specifically for clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease patients: the sample lists participants with “frontotemporal dementia (FTD)” but does not specify behavioral-variant FTD or provide a bvFTD-only group (I4 not met). Consequently, there are no between-group whole-brain contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met), and no group-level whole-brain results clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD sample (I7 not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails to meet I4, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical VBM study that reports voxelwise group contrasts with coordinates comparing FTD patients to controls. Imaging modality: VBM (meets I3). Sample: includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients meeting Neary criteria and behavioral descriptions consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (meets I4). Sample sizes exceed thresholds (32 patients total, 27 with usable MRI; 47 controls) satisfying I5. The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts (overeating FTD subgroup vs nonovereaters and controls) with stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach reported), satisfying I6 and I8. VBM analyses are voxelwise/group-level whole-brain comparisons within an a priori ROI and results are clearly identified as coming from the target patient group (meets I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only without voxelwise results, not only FC/DTI/thickness, and no disqualifying comorbid sample issues). Note: the authors use the term “FTD” and Neary criteria rather than explicitly ‘bvFTD’; behavioral descriptions and diagnostic criteria indicate behavioral-variant FTD, which slightly reduces but does not preclude inclusion. Overall confidence 0.85.

This study used FDG-PET (I3 satisfied) and included an FTLD patient group of n=11 (I5 satisfied). However it does not report clinically labeled bvFTD/Pick’s disease explicitly (I4 not clearly met), and crucially it does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to healthy controls; results are reported as regional/ROI hypometabolism counts and pattern descriptions rather than voxelwise coordinates (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI/regional analyses without whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical study that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons in MNI space. It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=13) and healthy controls (n=12), meeting sample-size requirements. The paper provides between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs. controls) with anatomical localization and MNI coordinates, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results and neuroanatomical correlates of emotional memory. The full text includes introduction, methods (VBM acquisition and preprocessing), results (group VBM comparisons and correlations) and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

Although the study used FDG-PET (meets I3), it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain between-group contrast specifically for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). The FTLD sample is pooled (FTD N=3, SD N=6, mixed N=4) and the paper presents comparisons of FTLD (pooled) and AD versus SCI controls rather than a separate bvFTD (FTD) versus control contrast. The number of bvFTD/FTD cases is only 3 (<6), so the bvFTD patient group does not meet the minimum sample size (I5). Therefore the study fails I4 (target sample not separably reported as bvFTD), I5 (bvFTD group <6), I6 (no bvFTD-vs-control whole-brain contrast where bvFTD are not pooled), and I7 (no whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target group).

Study uses VBM and includes a clinically defined FTD (bvFTD) subgroup (n=47) and healthy controls (n=43), meeting imaging and sample-size criteria. However, the neuroimaging analyses report whole-brain voxelwise correlations of interpersonal traits across a mixed diagnostic sample and co-atrophy checks; the paper does not present any between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast or group-level VBM result specifically comparing the bvFTD (FTD variant) group to controls in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I7 (bvFTD-specific between-group, whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Excluded on the basis of missing bvFTD-specific whole-brain between-group results.

This is an empirical VBM study that compares a clinically defined frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patient group (behaviorally defined FTD; patients with predominant behavioral/frontal syndrome, excluding progressive aphasia/semantic dementia) to healthy controls using whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses. Imaging modality is VBM (I3). The patient sample includes 9 FTD participants and 26 controls, meeting the minimum N≥6 for both groups (I5). Between-group voxelwise contrasts are reported in stereotactic space (SPM coordinates; e.g., periaqueductal gray at (0,-28,-10)) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are presented and attributed to the FTD sample (I6, I7). Results are reported as corrected and uncorrected voxelwise findings and coordinates (I8). No exclusion criteria (reviews-only, ROI-only, non-empirical, DTI/FC/CTh-only, or prohibited comorbid-sample) are met. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral/dysexecutive FTLD subgroup (bvFTLD) with n=71 and an imaging subset bvFTLD n=51 (I4, I5); reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts in MNI space comparing bvFTLD to healthy controls (contrasted with ~42 controls) and provides peak coordinates/tables and figures (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment of voxelwise whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness only, and comorbidities were excluded per methods).

The study reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (31 patients) (I4) with an adequate sample size (31 bvFTD; 56 controls) meeting the ≥6 participant threshold (I5). It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls and reports results on the Montreal Neurological Institute standard brain (MNI) with statistical parametric maps and coordinate-based tables/figures (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-FC/DTI/cortical-thickness only, and no evidence of disallowed comorbid sample). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical study that used task-based BOLD fMRI and voxel-based morphometric (VBM) volumetric MRI analyses comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls. The sample includes 16 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 16 healthy seniors (both ≥6). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts (bvFTD vs. controls) using SPM8 with FDR-corrected thresholds and cluster extent, and presents overlapping ROIs and coordinates (reported in figures/tables) in a standard stereotactic space. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The study uses task-based fMRI (n-back) and includes 7 FTD patients, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group results with Talairach coordinates (supplementary tables). However, it does not explicitly state that the patient sample is behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not clearly met). Also, the between-group contrasts reported compare FTD to Alzheimer’s disease patients rather than to healthy controls; inclusion criterion I6 requires a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls. Therefore not all required inclusion criteria are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM as imaging modality), I5 (FTD patient group n=29 and control group n=12, both ≥6), I7 (reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM group-level results in Talairach space). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (paper does not explicitly state inclusion of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD/bvFTD or Pick’s disease; FTD sample is described as heterogeneous subgroups including primary progressive aphasia and a subgroup with “disorder of social and executive functioning,” but bvFTD is not explicitly identified), I6 (no between-group contrast reported specifically for a bvFTD-only group versus controls; results are reported for the pooled FTD group). No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) are triggered. Because the review targets bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts, lack of an isolated bvFTD group/contrast prevents inclusion.

This study is excluded because it does not include a clinically defined behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease group as required by the review (inclusion criterion I4). Instead, participants are classified by pathological subtype (FTLD‐T and FTLD‐U) and while the majority “presented clinically as frontotemporal dementia,” the paper does not clearly define or isolate a bvFTD clinical group nor report between-group voxelwise contrasts specifically for a bvFTD group versus controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I5 (patient groups have ≥6 participants; controls n=61), I8 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (does not specify clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease group), I6 (no between-group contrast reported specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls in standardized stereotactic space), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging-analysis and sample-type requirements for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG‑PET was used), I5 (patient group size = 8 ≥ 6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are described as FTD but the paper does not explicitly state they are clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD [bvFTD] or Pick’s disease), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinates are reported). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the paper does not present whole-brain voxelwise results; imaging is used for diagnostic/illustrative purposes rather than reporting voxelwise, coordinate-based group comparisons). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Given the absence of explicit bvFTD sampling and lack of whole-brain voxelwise between-group coordinates/results, the study cannot be included in the coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is an empirical VBM study (SPM99 voxelwise analyses) reporting whole-brain, group-level contrasts in Talairach space. The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD subgroups, including a NON-APH subgroup described as having social/behavioral and executive impairment (behavioral-variant–type presentation) with n=14. Imaging/control group sizes meet the >=6 threshold (NON-APH n=14; imaging controls n=12). The paper reports subgroup VBM results (FTD subgroups vs healthy seniors) with coordinates and figures/tables (Table 4, Fig.2) so bvFTD-relevant whole-brain contrasts are provided and not pooled with other diagnoses. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s required target diagnosis. Although it uses FDG-PET (I3) and appears to have sufficient group sizes (I5), the patient sample is described as heterogeneous FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration) without specification that participants were clinically diagnosed with behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. Consequently, the paper does not report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts specifically comparing a bvFTD (or Pick’s disease) group to controls (I6 and I7 are not satisfied for the target sample). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered by the full text. Summary: exclusion IDs met: none; inclusion IDs met: I3, I5; inclusion IDs not met: I4, I6, I7. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet imaging-modality inclusion criterion I3: it uses SPECT (99mTc-ECD) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD, i.e., bvFTD/fvFTD), I5 (patient group n=48; control group n=15), I6 (reports voxel coordinates in MNI space), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results), I8 (results reported with coordinates and described in text). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This VBM study of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) meets several inclusion criteria: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients with early prominent behavioural features consistent with bvFTD within the sample), I5 (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls), and I8 (reports whole-brain results in tables/figures). However it does NOT meet key meta-analysis requirements: I6 and I7 are not satisfied because the paper does not report a between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group to healthy controls — instead analyses are performed on the mixed FTLD cohort (13 FTD + 3 SD) or on behavioural covariates within that pooled group. Therefore the target sample (bvFTD) is not isolated for a between-group voxelwise contrast, so the study cannot be included. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) .

This study reports FDG-PET (I3) on a clinically diagnosed frontal/behavioral variant FTD sample (bvFTD; I4). Imaging results are voxelwise SPM whole-brain analyses reported with Talairach coordinates and cluster statistics comparing patient groups to healthy controls (satisfies I6, I7, I8). PET subgroup sizes meet the minimum (H1 N=31, H2 N=10, controls N=16), and whole-brain between-group contrasts (H1 vs controls, H2 vs controls, and H1 vs H2) are reported, with coordinates provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the review.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=15) (I4) and healthy controls (n=20) with adequate sample sizes (>6) (I5). The paper reports between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls and provides whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space, including tables/figures of atrophy patterns and coordinates (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are met (no review/meta-analysis only, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness only, and sample comorbidities are exclusionary criteria but are not present).

This study is excluded because it does not provide the required whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results comparing a clearly identified bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group to controls in stereotactic space. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET was used) and I5 (patient group size for FTD = 17, which is ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (paper reports ‘FTD’ but does not explicitly state clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no between-group contrast results reported as coordinates in MNI/Talairach comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no clearly reported whole-brain, voxelwise group-level result from the target sample), and I8 (no coordinate tables/figures of whole-brain results for bvFTD). Exclusion criteria applied: E6 (the study presents diagnostic accuracy and region/volume-of-interest/3D-SSP descriptions without reporting whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the key disease-sample and contrast requirements for inclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (voxel-based morphometry was used) and I5 (patient groups, e.g., FTLD n=55, exceed the minimum of 6 participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the sample does not report a clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease group specifically — participants are classified by pathological FTLD subtypes rather than a bvFTD clinical subgroup), I6 (no between-group contrast is reported specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space — reported contrasts are for FTLD/FTLD subgroups, not bvFTD), and I7 (there is no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample). Exclusion criteria met: none (no applicable exclusion criteria such as review-only, ROI-only, DTI/FC-only, comorbid sample, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete. Because the review requires results specifically for clinically defined bvFTD (or Pick’s) groups and voxelwise between-group contrasts for that group, this paper cannot be included.

This study is excluded because it does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4 not met) and it does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in a standard space comparing a bvFTD patient group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). It instead studies presymptomatic genetic mutation carriers and uses classification on region-averaged features and TBSS/atlas-based tract averages rather than reporting whole-brain voxelwise group-level results; therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI/tract-summary analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI used) and I5 (sample sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no clinically diagnosed bvFTD/picks patients in the target sample), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space for bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result from target sample). Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain analyses performed in Montreal Neurologic Institute (MNI) space (I3, I7). The sample comprises clinically diagnosed frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) patients including a social/comportment & executive dysfunction subgroup (SOC/EXEC) consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) (I4). Sample sizes meet thresholds (40 patients total; MRI subgroup n=32; 27 healthy controls) (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts (patients/subgroups vs controls) with peak voxels/tables and figures in MNI space (I6, I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet imaging and whole-brain reporting criteria required for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (participants: clinically diagnosed FTD patients per Neary criteria, with semantic dementia and PNFA excluded, consistent with bvFTD sampling) and I5 (sample sizes: FTD n=44, controls present). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality) — the study used structural MRI lobar volumetry and automated regional volumes, not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET; I6 (between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach) — no voxelwise coordinate-based group contrasts are reported; I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level result from target sample) — not provided. Exclusion criteria triggered: E6 (reports only ROI/lobar analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The study uses whole-brain VBM and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=58) with controls (n=44), but its reported voxelwise analyses are brain–behavior correlations across a pooled neurodegenerative sample rather than between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls. The paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result clearly identified as coming solely from the bvFTD group (no bvFTD vs control contrast in MNI/Talairach space reported). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 despite meeting I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (probable bvFTD) (I4); has adequate sample size (44 patients, 60 controls) exceeding the 6-participant minimum (I5); reports group-level VBM comparisons of bvFTD versus controls (whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts consistent with VBM methods) satisfying between-group contrast reporting in standard (voxelwise) space (I6); and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results identified as coming from the bvFTD group (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply: this is an empirical study (not a review), reports whole-brain VBM (not ROI-only), participants had no major comorbid psychiatric/neurological disorders, and it does not only report seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because, although it uses VBM (I3) and includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s patients (I4), it does not report a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group (not pooled with other FTD subtypes) to controls in stereotactic coordinates. Thus it fails I6 and I7. The bvFTD subgroup sample size for a standalone bvFTD vs control contrast is not reported clearly, so I5 is not confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants within the sample: 47 bvFTD), and I5 (sample sizes: bvFTD n=47, controls n=34, both ≥6). However it does NOT meet I6 and I7: the published whole-brain VBM results are correlational analyses within the combined FTD patient sample (atrophy correlated with happiness behavior) rather than a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. No group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported that are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group alone (bvFTD results are not presented as an independent between-group contrast vs controls). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet I6 and I7.

The study is excluded because it reports only ROI/parcellation-based metabolic connectivity analyses (60 AAL VOIs) and does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise, coordinate-based (MNI/Talairach) between-group contrasts for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) versus controls. The FTLD group is analyzed as a pooled group including behavioral and language variants, and bvFTD-specific results are not reported separately. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I4 (includes behavioral-variant FTLD patients within the sample), I5 (sample sizes meet minimums). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group, coordinate-based voxelwise contrasts reported comparing bvFTD separately to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports only ROI/parcellation-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study used manual region-of-interest volumetry (manual cortical parcellation) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it reports ROI volumetric comparisons rather than whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotaxic coordinate space. This violates inclusion criteria I3 (required imaging modalities), I6 and I7 (required between-group voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach and whole-brain evidence). The study meets I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6). The sample is described as FTD but not explicitly as behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease, so I4 is not clearly satisfied. Exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses without whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4 (not specified as bvFTD), I6, I7. Exclusion criteria applied: E6. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

EXCLUDED: The study uses FDG-PET (I3) and has adequate group sizes (FTLD n=13; controls n=10) meeting I5, but it does not report data specifically from clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease—patients are described as FTLD without specification of bvFTD (I4 not met). Although voxelwise, whole-brain analyses are reported for FTLD vs controls, the paper does not provide results that can be clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD group, nor does it present between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) for a bvFTD group (I6, I7 not met). Coordinate reporting or bvFTD-specific whole-brain results are not present in the provided full text (I8 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered (none applicable). Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: imaging modality is FDG-PET (I3); the sample comprises clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients per Lund–Manchester criteria with other FTLD variants (semantic dementia, non-fluent progressive aphasia) excluded, consistent with a behavioral-variant FTD sample (I4) — diagnosis based on clinical criteria and PET pattern; sample sizes meet minimums (29 patients, 16 controls) (I5); the paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing FTD to controls with coordinates reported in Talairach/MNI space (I6); whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM results are clearly identified as coming from the patient group (I7); results are reported as coordinates/figures and described in text (I8). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria were met.

This is an empirical 18F-FDG PET study using voxel-wise SPM analysis (whole-brain) comparing 29 clinically diagnosed FTD patients to 11 healthy controls. The sample (n=29) meets the minimum size, and the authors explicitly excluded language variants (progressive nonfluent aphasia, semantic dementia), indicating the sample represents behavioral/clinical FTD cases. Analyses were performed in stereotactic space (normalized to MNI and coordinates converted to Talairach) and report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (Table 3 and figures). All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, no disallowed modalities). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=28) (I4), and meets sample-size requirements for patients and controls (I5), it does not present any between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group directly to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met). The VBM results are regression-based across a pooled, mixed-diagnosis sample (polisher/neutral and tarnisher/neutral analyses) and do not report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results coming specifically from the bvFTD subgroup (I7 not met). Full text appears complete.

The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise FDG-PET SPM analyses comparing FTD groups to controls and has adequate sample sizes (FTD n=29; controls n=11; FTD/MND n=8). However, the paper does not explicitly state that the patient sample consists of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease. The diagnostic label used is the consensus clinical diagnostic criteria for FTD (Neary et al.), but subtype breakdown (bvFTD vs other FTD variants) is not provided for the main FTD group. Inclusion criterion I4 (explicit bvFTD or Pick's disease sample) is therefore not met, and I6 (a between-group contrast explicitly of bvFTD versus controls) cannot be confirmed. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are triggered.

This study uses FDG-PET and includes >6 FTD patients overall, but it does not specifically report clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease as a clearly identified target group (I4 not met). The paper reports multivariate classification/discriminative images after MNI normalization, but it does not provide an explicit between-group voxelwise contrast (with coordinates) that compares a bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met). It is therefore not possible to confirm that a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result from a bvFTD-only sample is reported (I7 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET modality) and I5 (sample sizes >=6 across groups). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because key inclusion criteria I4, I6, and I7 are not satisfied.

This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (FTD subgroup) (I4), has adequate sample sizes (17 patients, 9 controls) exceeding the minimum of 6 per group (I5), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM group analyses comparing FTD and SD to controls (unpooled FTD vs controls) (I6,I7). The paper presents voxelwise, whole-brain results (BA labels and cluster reporting) and refers to tables/figures for coordinates, which satisfies acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion provided.

The study reports VBM and DTI analyses in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and controls with MNI coordinates provided (I3, I4, I5, I6 satisfied). However, the imaging analyses were conducted using an ROI mask confined to predefined motor-system regions rather than reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results. Therefore it does not provide whole-brain voxelwise results from the target sample (I7 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This study uses voxelwise structural MRI analysis (RAVENS/voxel-based methods) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results, includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (including behavioral variant cases), and has adequate sample sizes (12 patients, 12 controls). However, the FTD group is pooled across subtypes (behavioral/executive, language variants, corticobasal), and the manuscript does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast specifically isolating a bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) subgroup versus controls. Therefore it fails Inclusion Criterion I6 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups in reported results). No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Full text appears complete.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=84) and uses whole-brain VBM (I3, I4, I5 satisfied) and reports voxelwise results/coordinates (I8 satisfied), it does not report any between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls (no control group or bvFTD-vs-control voxelwise contrast). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (bvFTD vs controls contrast) and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise result originating from the bvFTD vs control comparison). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered.

Although this empirical paper uses VBM (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed frontal variant FTD subgroup (behavioral variant FTLD/FTD) with n=14 and a control group with n=20 (I4, I5 satisfied), it does not report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space that isolates the bvFTD (FTD) group versus controls. The VBM analyses reported are correlational (brain volume correlated with antisaccade performance) and, importantly, the primary VBM models controlled for or used a combined FTLD group (FTD+SD+PA) rather than presenting a direct bvFTD (FTD) >/< control voxelwise contrast. Therefore the study fails to meet I6 and I7 (no bvFTD-specific whole-brain between-group voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: none.

Excluded because study does not meet key inclusion criteria for a bvFTD-focused voxelwise meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I5 (patient group n=14 ≥6; control comparator n=33). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are described as pathologically confirmed FTLD but not specified as clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick's disease), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results or coordinate tables provided). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports regional visual/ROI-based assessments of predefined cortical regions rather than whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is ineligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on bvFTD voxelwise whole-brain results.

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=21) and healthy controls (n=25), uses voxel-based morphometry and whole-brain ICA/dual-regression voxelwise analyses in MNI space, and reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (including MNI coordinates). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

The paper reports a voxel-based morphometry (VBM) study with whole‑brain, voxelwise permutation analyses (MNI space) comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to healthy controls. MRI-based analyses used 9 bvFTD patients (MRI available) and an independent control group (35 healthy seniors) and report group GM density contrasts and voxelwise regressions relating atrophy to behavior. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets imaging modality (VBM), clinical sample (bvFTD), sample size (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls for imaging analyses), between‑group voxelwise contrasts in a defined stereotactic space, and whole‑brain group‑level results. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study uses VBM and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (16 bvFTD within 26 FTLD patients) and 21 healthy controls, and the patient and control sample sizes meet minimum thresholds. However the imaging analyses reported are voxelwise regression associations between grey matter and emotion-recognition performance within a combined FTLD cohort (and VBM was performed on FTLD patients only). The paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to controls in standard stereotactic space, nor does it present bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not provide results specific to the target clinical group (bvFTD). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I5 (patient and control groups exceed 6 subjects), I8 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not clearly report that participants are clinically-diagnosed bvFTD specifically; sample is mixed FTD phenotypes), I6 (no between-group contrast presented that compares a bvFTD-only group to controls in stereotactic space). Although whole-brain VBM analyses are reported for FTD and GRN+ vs GRN- comparisons, these are not specific to bvFTD and the bvFTD subgroup is neither isolated nor reported in coordinate-based contrasts. No exclusion criteria from the list (E5-E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Full text is complete and the study does include VBM (I3), clinically diagnosed bv-FTD participants (n=15) (I4), and adequate group sizes with controls (I5). However, it does NOT report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast that isolates the bvFTD group versus controls in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The VBM results presented compare a subgroup defined by poor melody scores to controls and report correlations across pooled patient groups; they do not provide a bvFTD-specific voxelwise contrast or coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because the paper lacks bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space (I6 and I7 not satisfied).

This is an empirical study that used FDG-PET (and ASL-MRI) and included a clearly clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=32) with cognitively normal controls (n=15). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (GLM and PLS logistic regression) with images normalized to a template and presents group-level voxelwise results contrasting bvFTD vs. controls and bvFTD vs. AD (figures and voxelwise analyses). The sample sizes exceed the minimum, and results are presented as whole-brain voxelwise maps (figures and statistical parametric maps) suitable for inclusion. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the record appears complete.

This study reports 18F-FDG PET voxelwise (SPM99) comparisons between a clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FTD) group (n=25) and healthy controls (n=15). The FTD group was diagnosed per revised Lund-Manchester criteria, with clinical features and selection (exclusion of primary progressive aphasia) consistent with the behavioral variant presentation. Imaging modality (FDG-PET), sample sizes, and independent group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with Talairach coordinates are provided for the FTD vs control contrast (FTD not pooled with SD). No exclusion criteria are met. Caveat: the paper uses the term “FTD” rather than explicitly “bvFTD,” but the clinical description, diagnostic criteria, and exclusion of PPA indicate the sample corresponds to behavioral-variant FTD. Therefore it meets required inclusion criteria for the review.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and result-reporting inclusion criteria and reports only region-based volumetric analyses. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes Pick's disease patients, n=17, as a pathological group) and I5 (patient group n=132 and control group n=107, both >6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is T1-weighted structural MRI volumetry/segmentation of amygdala subnuclei, not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast results reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates comparing bvFTD to controls — results are volumetric ROI comparisons and pathology/genetic subgroup comparisons), and I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results identified for the target sample). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded per the review criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain stereotactic reporting requirements. It used a linear MRI measure (Bifrontal Index) on structural T1 slices rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The sample is diagnosed as FTD using Neary criteria but the paper does not explicitly state behavioral-variant FTD or Pick's disease (I4 not met). No between-group voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (I6 and I7 not met). The study reports only a linear/region-like measure (BFI) rather than whole-brain voxelwise results, which falls under exclusion criterion E6. The study does meet the sample-size requirement (I5: patient group n=23). Inclusion criteria met: I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4, I6, I7. Exclusion criteria applied: E6. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Excluded because the study does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise results specific to a bvFTD group (bvFTD subgroup = 5 subjects). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD patients were included in the sample), I5 (overall patient group n=15 and control group n=12 meet the >=6 requirement), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported that compares a bvFTD-only group to controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other FTD subtypes) and I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target sample). No exclusion criteria were triggered (none of E5–E9 apply). Because the meta-analysis objective targets bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts (unpooled bvFTD group) and this study only reports mixed-FTD contrasts or subgroup analyses where the bvFTD cell has n<6, it does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this review.

This FDG-PET study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients and meets imaging modality (I3), includes FTD (behavioral syndrome) patients (I4), and has sufficient patient numbers (I5). However, it does not report a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD (or FTD) to healthy controls: the main voxelwise comparisons are FTLD+UIC vs FTLD−UIC, and subgroup analyses restricted to FTD compare incontinent vs continent FTD patients (no healthy control group). Inclusion criteria I6 (bvFTD vs controls contrast) and I7 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise result originating from a bvFTD vs control contrast) are not met. The FTD-restricted results did not survive correction and are reported only uncorrected, and the primary analyses pooled FTLD subtypes. Therefore it does not satisfy the review’s requirement for bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrasts. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within FTLD sample), I5 (patient group N=37, >6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported comparing a bvFTD group versus healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space—the VBM contrasts compare musicophilic vs non-musicophilic FTLD subgroups, not bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target sample). Exclusion criteria: none met. Therefore exclude because the study does not provide the required bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain between-group contrasts (I6/I7).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements. Exclusion criterion met: E6 (reports ROI/volumetric analyses and no whole-brain voxelwise statistical results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (participants clinically diagnosed with bvFTD), I5 (patient group n≥6 and control group n≥6 for imaging). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET; study used structural MRI volumetry/FreeSurfer/BSI and fluid registration), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in MNI/Talairach space with coordinates), I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results identified for the target sample). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded.

Study uses FDG-PET (I3 satisfied). However it does not provide data specific to clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease: the FTLD group includes 13 patients with only 3 labelled as 'FTD' (not specified as bvFTD), so there is no distinct bvFTD group (I4 not met). The bvFTD-relevant subgroup size is <6 (FTD n=3), so the sample-size criterion for the target group is not met (I5 not met). The reported between-group voxelwise contrasts are for aggregated FTLD (vs subjective cognitive impairment) rather than a bvFTD group unpooled from other diagnoses, so there is no between-group contrast specific to bvFTD (I6 not met) and no whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a single-case clinical genetic case report of childhood-onset cerebellar ataxia due to a homozygous SQSTM1 mutation, not a study of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (violates I3); the sample does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease patients (violates I4); patient group size is N=1, below the required minimum of 6 (violates I5); no between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls are reported (violates I6); and no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results from a target bvFTD sample are presented (violates I7/I8). No exclusion criteria from the list are specifically met. Therefore the study does not satisfy the required inclusion criteria for this review and is excluded.

The provided full text is a corrigendum (funding correction) only and does not include core article content (introduction, methods, results). Therefore I cannot verify any required inclusion criteria. Specifically: inclusion criteria not met/uncertain - I3 (imaging modality: VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET) not reported; I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick's disease sample) not confirmed; I5 (sample sizes ≥6) not reported; I6 (between-group MNI/Talairach coordinates for bvFTD vs controls) not reported; I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level result) not reported; I8 (format of whole-brain results) not verifiable. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (the provided document is a non-empirical corrigendum without original data). Because the full text is incomplete (corrigendum only), the study cannot be assessed against the review criteria and is excluded.

This full-text reports an empirical voxel-based morphometry (VBM) study (FSL VBM) examining dementia groups including a clearly defined behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) subgroup (n=11). Controls (n=15) meet the control sample size requirement. The manuscript describes voxel-wise, whole-brain t-tests comparing each patient group (behavioural-variant FTD, semantic dementia, PNFA, Alzheimer’s disease) to controls, reports results overlaid on the MNI standard brain and provides cluster coordinates (voxelwise MNI space). Analyses specifically examine bvFTD (patterns of atrophy and correlations in bvFTD combined with controls), and results are presented as whole-brain voxelwise findings (figures/tables/supplementary). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Meets all inclusion criteria for the review: (I3) uses VBM; (I4) includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=16); (I5) sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTD=16, controls=18); (I6) reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI space (controls>FTD, FTD>PSP, etc.) where bvFTD is not pooled; (I7) provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise VBM results; (I8) whole-brain results are described in text/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, empirical data, no comorbid psychiatric/neuro disorders reported). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons (FTLD/FTD vs controls) with coordinates in standardized space (MNI) and corrected results, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements (I6,I7,I8). The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD (behavioral variant/frontotemporal dementia) as a distinct subgroup (FTD n=15) within FTLD (I4), with adequate group sizes (FTLD n=25 total; VBM available in 21 FTLD and 17 controls) exceeding the minimum of 6 per group (I5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, VBM analyses and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered: this is not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and it does not use excluded modalities. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports voxelwise FDG-PET analyses in a sample of 29 clinically diagnosed FTD patients (PPA and semantic dementia explicitly excluded), with age-matched controls. The methods use SPM in MNI space and report group-level, whole-brain results (conjunction and subtraction analyses) including MNI coordinates (e.g., 4,62,-6; Z=7.03). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (29 patients; controls per center ≥6). The analyses are whole-brain voxelwise (not ROI-only) and the bvFTD-like clinical phenotype (behavioral/social disinhibition, loss of insight) is consistent with behavioral-variant FTD. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review/meta-analysis, ROI-only, seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness only) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

The study uses whole-brain VBM and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=20) and healthy controls (n=13), but it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD group directly to controls in MNI/Talairach space. The reported VBM analyses are correlational across a mixed diagnostic sample and regression analyses controlling for diagnosis, not a group-level bvFTD vs control coordinate-based contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7.

Study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons in MNI space comparing clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD subjects to matched controls. Patient sample size (n=17 total; 7 with stereotypies, 10 without) and control group (matched, n≈17) both exceed the minimum of 6. The paper provides whole-brain group-level results (FTLD vs controls and direct FTLD subgroup comparisons) and details preprocessing in MNI space. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (systematic review, ROI-only, non-empirical, exclusively other modalities, or problematic comorbid samples) are met.

This study is excluded because it does not provide bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results with an adequate bvFTD sample. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses resting-state fMRI) and I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (bvFTD subgroup N=4, which is <6 required), I6 (no reported between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls—the paper reports an aggregated FTD group and discusses FTD subtypes pooled), and I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample alone). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. The full text appears complete. Because the meta-analysis objective specifically targets bvFTD and requires bvFTD-specific, whole-brain contrasts with sufficient sample size, this study must be excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for bvFTD and AD groups; (I4) included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=21) per revised criteria; (I5) sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTD n=21; controls n=20); (I6) reported between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (two-sample t-tests) without pooling bvFTD with other groups; (I7) provided whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results for bvFTD (reported atrophy patterns from VBM, p<0.001 uncorrected, extent threshold=50 voxels); (I8) whole-brain results are described in text and referenced figures/tables/supplementary materials. No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, no disallowed imaging modalities, and participants excluded for other psychiatric/neurological diagnoses). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (64 bvFTD cases) and adequate sample size, but it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements of the review. The primary analyses use automated regional volumetry/atlas-based regional volumes and derived indices (API, ASI, TPL) rather than VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET as the main imaging modality (I3 not met). Although an exploratory voxel-based morphometry (VBM) cluster analysis is mentioned, the paper does not present clear whole-brain, standard-space (MNI/Talairach) between-group voxelwise contrasts for the overall bvFTD group versus controls (or clearly tabulated coordinates), so criteria requiring at least one between-group contrast in a defined stereotactic space (I6) and at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample (I7) are not clearly satisfied. Therefore the study should be excluded for not meeting I3, I6, and I7.

The study uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and has adequate group sizes (14 patients, 12 controls) (I5). However, the analyses are ROI-based (AAL atlas) with graph-theory Network Centrality metrics and do not report whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Thus inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. This meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=17) and healthy controls (n=22). The study uses task fMRI (satisfying I3), includes a bvFTD group (I4) with >=6 participants and a control group >=6 (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses (SPM) with between-group contrasts and syndrome-specific results described for bvFTD versus controls (e.g., reduced posterior middle temporal and fusiform activation), meeting I6 and I7. Results are presented as whole-brain SPMs and described in the text/figures (I8). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract provided) and the study does not use required neuroimaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) nor report whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (patient group N=12 >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is clinical MRI visual ratings, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Because key imaging and whole-brain coordinate requirements are not satisfied, exclude.

This is a retrospective clinical case series (n=21) using CT, structural MRI (NMR), and SPECT perfusion imaging; it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The study lacks a healthy/control group and reports no between-group contrasts in a standardized coordinate space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to controls (I6 not met). No whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results for the target sample are reported (I7 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (patient group n=21 ≥6). Exclusion criteria met: E7 (the sample includes concurrent psychiatric symptoms: depressive and psychotic symptoms reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails key imaging and analysis inclusion criteria and includes comorbid psychiatric symptoms.

This study uses VBM (I3 satisfied), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=19) (I4 satisfied) and has adequate group sizes (bvFTD n=19; controls n=21) (I5 satisfied). However, the VBM analyses reported are within-patient-group voxelwise correlations of grey matter with behavioural/EMG measures rather than between-group voxelwise contrasts directly comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in standard space. Therefore it does not provide the required between-group (bvFTD vs controls) whole-brain voxelwise contrast in MNI/Talairach coordinates (I6 not met) nor a clear whole-brain group-level between-group result from the target sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (n=25 bvFTD, n=21 controls), I7 (reports group-level voxelwise VBM results derived from the target bvFTD sample) and I8 (results presented in tables/figures). However, it does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast directly comparing bvFTD versus controls in MNI/Talairach space (no whole-brain bvFTD>control or control>bvFTD contrast is presented), so inclusion criterion I6 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and adequate sample sizes (patients and controls), but it does not report a between-group whole-brain VBM contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls. Instead, the imaging analysis reports voxelwise correlates of PCA-derived behavioral components across a transdiagnostic patient sample (and correlations with component scores), not an isolated bvFTD vs control voxelwise group contrast in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and the requirement that at least one whole-brain group-level result be clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group (I7). Exclusion criteria: none met.

This is an empirical, full-text MRI volumetric study that included clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) with adequate group sizes (I5). However, the imaging modality is T1-weighted volumetric segmentation (thalamic volumes), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, so it does not meet I3. The paper reports region-of-interest (whole thalamus) volumetric comparisons using ANCOVA and ROC analyses rather than voxelwise, whole-brain results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach), therefore it does not meet I6 or I7. This means it performs ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results, invoking exclusion criterion E6. Summary: Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I6, I7. Exclusion criterion met: E6. Full text appears complete.

The study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry and reports MNI-coordinate results (satisfies I3, I7, I8). Patient and control group sizes meet the minimum (10 patients, 20 controls) (satisfies I5). However, the patient groups are mixed FTD subtypes (FTD/SQSTM1 carriers include 7 bvFTD and 3 PNFA; sporadic FTD also mixed) and all reported between-group contrasts compare these mixed FTD groups (SQSTM1 carriers or Sporadic FTD) to controls rather than a bvFTD-only group. Therefore it does not meet I4 (requires clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease sample) and I6 (requires a between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group, not pooled with other subtypes, to controls). No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG‑PET) and I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 — the bvFTD patient subgroup contains only 2 participants (total sample n=6 but only 2 bvFTD), below the required >=6; I6 — no group-level between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls is reported (analyses are single-subject SPM comparisons); I7 — no group-level whole‑brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD group is presented. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) appear to apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper cannot be included.

Although the study includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=20) and healthy controls (N=31), and uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses of grey matter (so I3, I4, I5 and I7 are met), it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space. Imaging analyses were conducted as within-bvFTD correlational analyses (behaviour–GM/DTI associations) rather than group-level bvFTD vs control contrasts. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because the neuroimaging results do not provide a between-group whole-brain contrast comparing bvFTD to controls (I6 not met). The VBM analysis reported (coordinates for left putamen) is from a correlational analysis within a pooled FTD sample (bvFTD + avPPA) rather than a bvFTD-versus-controls voxelwise group contrast; therefore it also fails I7 (a group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample alone). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM was used), I4 (bvFTD patients included), I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6), and I8 (whole-brain coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion reason: E6 (study reports ROI/parcellation-based network analyses with no voxelwise whole-brain (MNI/Talairach) coordinates). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample present, N=38), I5 (sample sizes: bvFTD n=38, controls n=32). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group results reported in a defined stereotactic space such as MNI or Talairach comparing bvFTD to controls—results are reported as ROI/node-based network components rather than peak coordinates), I7 (no voxelwise whole-brain group-level results clearly reported for the target group). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false. Summary: Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases and uses resting-state fMRI with adequate sample sizes, the analyses are ROI-based graph/network and NBS outputs (node indices and lobar connectivity weights) rather than voxelwise MNI/Talairach coordinate contrasts or tables; therefore it fails the meta-analysis requirements for whole-brain voxelwise coordinate data and must be excluded under E6.

This is an original, empirical, whole-brain voxelwise neuroimaging study that meets all inclusion criteria. It uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) alongside DTI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=12) separate from other FTD subtypes (I4) with adequate sample sizes (controls n=15; I5). The paper reports voxelwise between-group contrasts in standard space (MNI) for bvFTD versus controls (TBSS and VBM analyses; I6) and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (figures and text; I7, I8). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met.

Included imaging modality and samples: this study uses voxel-based morphometry (satisfies I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (11 patients) (satisfies I4), and has adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=11; controls n=22) (satisfies I5). However, the VBM analyses reported are associations across the combined patient cohort (AD, bvFTD, SD, PNFA) and regression-based correlations with musical performance; the paper does not present a voxelwise between-group contrast in standard space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTD group specifically to controls unpooled (I6 not met). Consequently, there is no clear group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) result identified as coming from the bvFTD sample alone (I7 not met). Full text appears complete. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7.

The study meets several inclusion criteria (uses VBM and resting-state fMRI; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; has sufficient sample sizes; reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM results in the bvFTD group with coordinates in tables). However, it does not report at least one between-group voxelwise contrast (bvFTD vs controls) in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach).
