Group-level comparisons reported are ROI/edge-based connectivity differences, not voxelwise coordinate-based between-group imaging contrasts. Thus inclusion criterion I6 is not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

While the study uses voxel-based morphometry (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=12) with healthy controls (n=17) satisfying sample size requirements (I4, I5), it does not report a between-group, voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group directly to controls in MNI/Talairach space. The neuroimaging results are voxelwise regressions of flavour identification across the patient cohort and associations within the bvFTD subgroup, but no explicit bvFTD vs control whole-brain between-group contrast is presented. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls) is not met, which is required for inclusion. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. No exclusion criteria were triggered.

The study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria: I3 (uses voxel-based morphometry), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants within the sample), I5 (bvFTD subgroup size = 12; controls = 30, both ≥6), I6 (reports between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD group to controls in SPM/MNI space), I7 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD subgroup), and I8 (results are described in text and shown in figures). No exclusion criteria are met (no review/meta-analysis, whole-brain VBM used rather than ROI-only, no disqualifying comorbidities reported, and not a methods-only paper). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Hence include.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD meta-analysis: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=15) (I4) and healthy controls (n=18) with sample sizes >6 (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) performed in standard space (MNI) with TFCE and permutation testing (I6,I7). Results are described in text and figures (I8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore INCLUDE.

The study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports voxelwise, family-wise-error corrected results with MNI coordinates. It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (N=50) and age-matched controls (total sample N reported and controls clearly >6). The paper reports syndrome-specific, whole-brain VBM contrasts involving the bvFTD group (syndrome-specific atrophy in bvFTD with MNI coordinates and figures/tables) and links findings to behavioral measures. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusions) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study should be excluded because it meets exclusion criterion E9: it reports only seed-based functional connectivity analyses (wSDM vs Pearson R) without VBM or FDG-PET. It nevertheless satisfies all inclusion criteria: I3 (resting-state fMRI modality), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants), I5 (adequate sample sizes: Country-1 final n=20 patients and 20 controls; Country-2 n=15 patients and 29 controls), I6 (between-group voxelwise contrasts using SPM reported for bvFTD vs controls), I7 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results reported), and I8 (results described in text/figures and supplementary material). No other exclusion criteria (E5–E8) are met. Full text appears complete.

The study reports voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (DTI TBSS and VBM) projected to standard MNI space and presents group-level contrasts comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group to healthy controls and to an AD group. The cohort includes 27 bvFTD patients and ≥6 participants in control groups (20 healthy, 25 AD). VBM (grey-matter voxel-based morphometry) is used in addition to DTI, satisfying the imaging modality requirement. Whole-brain results for the target bvFTD sample are clearly reported (FWE-corrected maps, intersection maps, and ROC analyses). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC only, and sample comorbidities do not violate exclusions).

This study uses voxel-based morphometry and FDG-PET with voxelwise (whole-brain) analyses (meets I3). However, it does not provide results specifically for a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (or Pick’s disease) group compared directly to controls. The sample is a mixed familial-FTLD cohort (various clinical syndromes including some bvFTD cases), and all reported voxelwise between-group contrasts are organized by amyloid status (A+ vs A− vs CN) rather than an isolated bvFTD vs control contrast. The paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain contrast that clearly and exclusively compares bvFTD patients to healthy controls, nor does it report the number of bvFTD-only participants reaching the required n≥6 for an isolated bvFTD group. Therefore it fails to meet I4, I6, and I7 (and I5 for a bvFTD-specific group). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study uses VBM on MRI and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (18 patients) and 18 controls, with whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons reported (controls > FTD), satisfying I3, I4, I5, I7 and I8. However, the provided full text does not report results in a defined stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach) or provide peak coordinates for the bvFTD vs control contrast, so it does not meet I6 (required reporting of between-group results in a defined stereotactic space). No exclusion criteria were met. Therefore the study must be excluded because not all inclusion criteria (specifically I6) are satisfied.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used voxel-based morphometry), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD group n=30, >6), I7 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise VBM results) and I8 (results presented in figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (study does NOT report any between-group contrast comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls; all reported group contrasts are between patient groups—bvFTD, SD, AD—or analyses collapsed/irrespective of diagnosis). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Because the study fails to meet I6 (required by the review), it must be excluded.

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD (N=19) with healthy controls (N=20). It uses voxel-based morphometry and task-based fMRI (meets I3). Sample meets diagnostic and size requirements (I4, I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group VBM results (two-sample t-test, FWE-corrected) and fMRI group analyses after normalization to MNI space, clearly reporting group-level whole-brain results comparing bvFTD to controls (I6, I7). Results are reported in the main text with full methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, includes whole-brain analyses, not limited to seed FC/DTI/cortical thickness, and sample lacks disqualifying comorbidities).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain coordinate reporting criteria required for the meta-analysis. Exclusion criteria met: E9 (study uses cortical thickness/volumetric Freesurfer analyses and does not report VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (has >=6 bvFTD patients in the sporadic bvFTD comparison group and >=6 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — uses Freesurfer volumetric/cortical thickness methods), I6 (does not report at least one between-group contrast in stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls), and I7 (no clearly identified group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported in stereotactic space with coordinates). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (SPM5) to perform whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons of clinically diagnosed bvFTD subjects (n=66) to age- and gender-matched controls (n=30), reporting group-level voxelwise results (FWE-corrected maps and direct subtype vs subtype contrasts). The methods and results sections provide whole-brain analyses and figures/tables describing between-group contrasts in standard neuroimaging space, and the sample sizes exceed the minimum threshold. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the paper meets the review inclusion requirements.

This empirical study directly investigates bvFTD and cerebro-cardiac control using resting-state fMRI and voxel-wise structural analyses. It reports clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=17–20) and healthy controls (n=19), meeting minimum sample-size requirements. The paper includes whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (e.g., bvFTD < HC HRV-BOLD coupling) with coordinate reporting and supplementary tables, and uses both seed-based intrinsic connectivity and whole-brain voxel-wise degree centrality (seed-independent) as well as voxel-wise structural lateralization analyses. No exclusion criteria are met: it is not a review/meta-analysis, provides whole-brain results (not ROI-only), and the sample is described without comorbid psychiatric diagnoses or substance abuse that would trigger exclusion. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is appropriate for inclusion in the review.

This study uses resting-state fMRI (meets I3) in a clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD sample (meets I4) with adequate sample sizes (18 patients, 50 controls; meets I5). However, the analyses are graph-theoretical/network-based using AAL parcellation and report regional/parcel-level network metrics and anatomical labels rather than voxelwise, whole-brain group contrasts reported in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The paper does not present between-group voxelwise coordinates or statistical maps in MNI/Talairach space; therefore it does not meet I6 and I7. Because the study reports only region/ROI-based network results without whole-brain voxelwise coordinates, it falls under exclusion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Consequently the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain bvFTD contrast requirements. Exclusion criterion E9 applies: the paper uses cortical-thickness/voxelwise GM maps processed with ANTs (antsCorticalThickness and antsLongitudinalCorticalThickness) rather than the required VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET modalities. Crucially, although the sample includes a bvFTD group (n=15) and controls (n=21) (I4 and I5 satisfied), the neuroimaging analyses and voxelwise whole-brain results are reported only for svPPA patients (cross-sectional and longitudinal comparisons) and regressions of svPPA GM change to concreteness; there are no group-level whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts reported for the bvFTD group versus controls (I6 and I7 not met). Full text appears complete.

This study uses FDG-PET (meets I3) but does NOT include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease patient group at the time of imaging (fails I4). The sample consists of MCI subjects, some of whom converted to FTD at follow-up, but there is no group of clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants analyzed as a distinct patient group. The paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD patient group to controls in standard stereotactic space with coordinates (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it does not provide the required between-group voxelwise results for bvFTD vs controls. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6, I7 (also I5 not applicable to a bvFTD patient group). No exclusion criteria from the review list were triggered.

Included imaging modalities and sample: The study uses resting-state fMRI and 18F-FDG PET (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (I4) with sufficient sample size (I5). However, the paper does not report any voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrast in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) that directly compares the bvFTD group to controls; instead, group comparisons are reported on ICA-derived network integrity/loading coefficients (summary indices) rather than voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for the bvFTD group) are not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Exclusion criteria: none of the exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, reviews) apply. Decision: EXCLUDED because I6 and I7 are not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: [].

This is an empirical imaging study that includes a clearly diagnosed bvFTD cohort and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext appears complete). The study used resting-state fMRI for RSN ICA analyses and VBM for grey-matter measurements (I3). It enrolled 15 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 15 healthy controls (I4, I5). Functional and structural data were spatially normalized to Talairach space and group-level, whole-brain contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls are reported (RS-fMRI network differences and VBM results) satisfying I6 and I7; whole-brain results are described in the text and figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed modalities, and sample exclusions not violated). Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

Study uses resting-state fMRI and includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients (I3, I4 satisfied). However, it does not report any between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts in standard space (MNI/Talairach) that isolate the bvFTD group versus controls (results are reported for FTD pooled [bvFTD+SD] vs controls and ROI-derived from that contrast). The bvFTD subgroup analyses reported are based on n=5 bvFTD patients (below the required minimum of 6), and no bvFTD-specific whole-brain coordinate results are provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met, and the bvFTD-specific sample size requirement of I5 is not met for the bvFTD subgroup. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an FDG‑PET study including clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=33) and controls (n=22), but the analyses focus on ROI-based PCC SUVr, visual reads, ROC and regression analyses. The paper does not report any whole‑brain voxelwise group results in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide coordinate tables/figures of voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls. Therefore it fails the requirements for voxelwise/whole‑brain reporting (I6, I7) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI/no whole‑brain results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although the study uses whole-brain VBM (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases within the FTD sample (17 bvFTD patients) satisfying the minimum sample-size requirements (I4, I5), the reported voxelwise whole-brain results are for the pooled FTD group (FTD = 52) and for AD vs controls. The paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts or coordinate results that are specific to the behavioral-variant FTD subgroup (bvFTD) alone. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and the requirement that at least one whole-brain result be clearly identified as coming from the target sample (I7). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not report a bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise contrast vs. controls (fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7). Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the sample (I4), and has sufficient overall patient (n=28) and control (n=50) sizes (I5), the VBM results are presented for FTLD-TDP pathological subtypes (type 1, 2, 3) rather than for a clinical bvFTD-only group. Therefore there is no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only sample for inclusion. Additionally, the study allowed comorbid Alzheimer disease and Lewy body pathologies, which meets exclusion criterion E7. Full text appears complete.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it used VBM and FDG-PET imaging (I3); included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (23 patients; I4) with adequate sample size and control groups (patients n=23; controls for MRI and PET >6; I5); reports between-group voxelwise contrasts versus controls in MNI space and provides cluster results/tables (I6); reports whole‑brain, group-level voxelwise results (VBM and PET) (I7) and results are clearly described in text/tables/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is an original empirical VBM/PET study (not a review), it reports whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), and does not rely solely on disallowed modalities. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore INCLUDE for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical study of bvFTD using structural MRI volumetry (Freesurfer) reporting ROI cortical volumes (orbitofrontal, middle frontal gyrus) and group comparisons, but it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The paper does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) nor coordinate tables/figures for such contrasts (I6 and I7 not met). It therefore only provides region-of-interest/volume analyses, so it meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only with no whole-brain results). Included: clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (I4) and sample sizes meet minimums (I5). Excluded because I3, I6, and I7 are not satisfied and E6 applies.

This is a clinical/protocolal overview of integrated FDG PET-MRI with illustrative cases and institutional experience, not an empirical group-level neuroimaging study. It does use FDG-PET (I3 satisfied) but does not present a diagnostically defined bvFTD sample with n≥6, nor any between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space, nor whole-brain voxelwise group-level results. Therefore it fails I4, I5, I6, and I7. The manuscript appears non-empirical/methods/report-style rather than reporting original quantitative group analyses (E8 applies). Full text appears complete.

Although this RCT includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses of the bvFTD sample and has adequate patient numbers, it does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD to healthy controls in a standard stereotactic space. The VBM comparison provided is between bvFTD and a parallel mild-AD cohort. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants), I5 (ample patient sample, n=220), I7 (reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level VBM results from the bvFTD sample), I8 (results presented in figure/text). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group contrast of bvFTD vs healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space where bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups). No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not use the imaging modalities required by the review (I3). The paper reports a visual MRI atrophy assessment rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it does not report any between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide coordinate results (I6 and I7 not met). It does meet inclusion criteria I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (sample size: 75 patients). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used VBM), I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (sample sizes: 24 bvFTD, 24 healthy controls), I7 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from the bvFTD sample), I8 (whole-brain results are described in text/figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (the paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast in stereotactic space directly comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls that is clearly presented as MNI/Talairach coordinates or a between-group SPM; the VBM analyses reported are within-group regression associations and comparisons across patient groups, not a direct bvFTD vs control voxelwise contrast). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I6 (required between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls).

Excluded because the study used only cortical thickness (surface-based FreeSurfer) analyses rather than one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), meeting exclusion criterion E9. The paper does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (bvFTD n=48) and adequate sample sizes with controls (meets I4 and I5). However it does not use the required imaging modalities (I3 not met) and does not report between-group results in a standardized stereotaxic coordinate space (MNI/Talairach) as required (I6 not met). It is also unclear that a standard voxelwise whole-brain statistical contrast in stereotaxic space for bvFTD vs controls is provided (I7 not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Although the paper includes VBM (I3), clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4, n=20), and adequate sample sizes for patient and control groups (I5), it does NOT report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The VBM analyses described and reported are correlations between BDNF serum concentrations and regional brain volume across subjects and report no significant correlations; no group-level bvFTD vs control voxelwise results or coordinate tables are provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample sizes and whole-brain voxelwise results. The paper uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on MRI (Methods: VBM, SPM8), includes clinically diagnosed probable/possible/pre-bvFTD patients confirmed at follow-up (n=194 total; VBM subset: 44 probable bvFTD, 19 possible bvFTD, 14 pre-bvFTD) and healthy controls (n=36). The study reports between-group whole-brain contrasts (probable bvFTD < HC; possible bvFTD < HC; pre-bvFTD < HC) with stereotactic coordinates for significant clusters (x,y,z values provided) and familywise error correction at whole-brain level. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, no disallowed imaging modality). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be included in the review.

This is not an imaging study using VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). While the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4 met) with adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=56; controls n=22; I5 met), the paper does not report any voxelwise, whole-brain group-level neuroimaging results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to controls (I6 and I7 not met). The study reports neuropsychological testing (FCSRT) and some amyloid PET for biomarker classification, but no suitable whole-brain VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET coordinates or voxelwise contrasts are provided. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I6, I7. No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) were triggered. Therefore exclude from this meta-analysis focused on whole-brain VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET contrasts of bvFTD versus controls.

This is a structural neuroimaging and postmortem study using manual ROI tracing of the hypothalamus and postmortem histology. Although it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and adequate sample sizes (neuroimaging: 18 patients, 16 controls; I5), it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The study reports ROI volumetric comparisons and postmortem cell counts rather than between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) and does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise coordinates (I6 and I7 not met). Because it reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results, it meets exclusion criterion E6. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study should be excluded. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only visual rating/region-based MRI assessments with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (patient group N=43, SD N=34, both >6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — uses visual rating scales on structural MRI), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in stereotaxic coordinates comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (no whole-brain coordinate tables/figures in stereotaxic space). Additionally, the provided full text appears to be an abstract/summary rather than a complete article; therefore fulltext_incomplete=true.

This study is excluded because, although it includes FDG-PET (I3), and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with at least 6 bvFTD cases (I5), it does not report any voxel-wise, whole-brain, group-level between-group contrasts comparing a bvFTD patient group to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The paper presents diagnostic biomarker results and descriptive PET patterns but no coordinate tables, voxelwise statistical maps, or between-group analyses meeting I6/I7. No whole-brain voxelwise results for bvFTD vs controls are provided, and no control group analyses are reported. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria (I6, I7) required for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E6. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD included; n=50), I5 (sample sizes: bvFTD n=50; controls n=32). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7. Although group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) and network differences are reported, the paper reports ROI-/node-based connectivity (AAL atlas seeds, seed-based FC, and network-based statistics/graph metrics) rather than whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results reported in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) with coordinates. No tables or coordinates in MNI/Talairach for voxelwise between-group contrasts are provided in the text supplied. Therefore the study provides only ROI/network-level connectivity findings and does not satisfy the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results; it must be excluded under E6.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (the sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural MRI with SIENA/SIENAX, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I5 (patient group size is 1 bvFTD participant, far below the required ≥6), I6 (no between-group statistical contrast reported in a defined stereotactic space such as MNI or Talairach comparing a bvFTD group to controls), and I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from the target bvFTD sample are provided). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are directly triggered by this report. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because multiple required inclusion criteria are not satisfied (notably I3, I5, I6, I7), the study must be excluded.

This study meets all inclusion requirements: it uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) (I4) with an adequate sample size and a healthy control group (n=30), both >6 participants (I5); reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts in standard (MNI) space comparing bvFTD to controls and to probable AD without pooling bvFTD with other groups (I6,I7). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext appears complete) and reports coordinate/voxelwise results (I8). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, seed-based-only, comorbid samples) are met. Therefore the paper is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical study of bvFTD (meets I4) with sufficient sample sizes (14 patients, 14 controls; meets I5). However, it does not use Voxel-Based Morphometry, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The paper reports MRI visual ratings of atrophy rather than voxelwise whole-brain imaging analyses with stereotactic coordinates, and it does not report any between-group contrasts in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) (I6 and I7 not met). Thus it provides no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables/figures suitable for the meta-analysis. Applicable exclusion criterion: E6 (only ROI/visual-rating or no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails required imaging and whole-brain result criteria (I3, I6, I7).

The study is excluded because it does not meet imaging-modality inclusion criterion I3: it uses deformation-based morphometry (DBM), not Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM), task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET. It does meet other inclusion criteria: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (sufficient sample size: 70 bvFTD, 133 controls), I6 (between-group contrasts registered to ICBM/MNI template), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level DBM results), and I8 (results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the reported content. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded solely for failing I3.

The study examines bvFTD and used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD proband (I4). It reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM results for the proband versus controls (I7). However, the patient sample consists of a single proband (N=1), so it fails the minimum sample-size requirement of at least 6 patients (I5). The report does not clearly present a between-group contrast in a defined stereotactic space with coordinates for a bvFTD group of adequate size (I6 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it does not meet I5 (and does not satisfy I6 for a group-level contrast in stereotactic coordinates).

This study uses structural MRI cortical thickness and volumetric analyses (FreeSurfer surface-based measures), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and therefore does not meet the modality inclusion (I3). Although clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants are present (C9+ bvFTD subgroup), the bvFTD patient subgroup has only 3 participants (<6), so I5 is not met. The paper reports surface-based vertex-wise results for symptomatic C9+ subjects but does not provide whole-brain voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) coordinate results for a bvFTD group specifically, so I6 and I7 are not satisfied. Thus the study is excluded under E9 (studies that report only cortical thickness methods). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (contains clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I5, I6, I7. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging- and analysis-related inclusion criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only ROI/volumetric analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; used FreeSurfer volumetric ROI measures), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in stereotactic coordinates [MNI/Talairach]), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper does not provide the required whole-brain, voxelwise coordinate results from an eligible imaging modality and must be excluded.

This empirical study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports group-level voxelwise comparisons between clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and healthy controls, with correlational VBM results linked to task performance. Sample sizes meet the minimum (18 bvFTD, 36 controls), and the paper reports whole-brain GM density differences and cluster-level correlations identified via SPM/VBM (reported as clusters and anatomically localized regions). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analyses, inappropriate imaging modality, comorbid psychiatric pooling) are met. Therefore the study satisfies the review’s imaging, sample, whole-brain reporting, and result-format requirements.

The study used resting-state fMRI and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and healthy controls (n=65), so I3, I4, and I5 are satisfied. However, the report is based on ROI/seed-based intrinsic connectivity and node-pair summary analyses and does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs. controls) in MNI/Talairach space or coordinate tables in the provided full text. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. This matches exclusion criteria E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E9 (reports seed-based functional connectivity rather than whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because no group-level whole-brain voxelwise coordinates/contrasts for bvFTD vs. controls were reported (violates I6/I7); exclusion criteria E6 and E9 apply.

This is an empirical study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=19) and controls, but it does not use VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET nor report group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in a stereotactic space. The paper reports behavioral moral-judgment results and lesion mapping of individual PFL patients to a standard brain, but no VBM or voxelwise between-group imaging results (MNI/Talairach) for the bvFTD group are provided. Therefore it fails the imaging and whole-brain reporting inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD sample present) and I5 (>=6 patients and controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modality), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in defined stereotactic space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from target sample). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Full text appears complete.

The study reports whole-brain VBM analyses (group comparison and within-patient regression) and FDG-PET data were acquired in most patients. The sample consists of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=20) and controls (N=20), meeting the minimum sample-size criterion. The paper presents voxelwise, group-level VBM results (a two-sample t-test comparing patients to controls) and reports MNI coordinates for the VBM regression peak (−41, 26, 3), indicating results are in a standard stereotactic space. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) in clinically-diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease subjects (I4), reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts with peak coordinates (I6, I7, I8). However, the patient groups used for the reported between-group contrasts are small (PiD n=5, CBD n=5, FTLD-TDP type 1 n=5), falling below the required minimum of 6 participants per patient group (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered (e.g., not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed modalities). Therefore the study is excluded solely because it fails inclusion criterion I5 (insufficient patient group size for reported contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Excluded because the bvFTD sample comprises patients with comorbid ALS (neurological disorder), violating exclusion criterion E7. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD subgroup present), I5 (patient group n=7, controls n=39 meet size thresholds), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise VBM results reported for the ALS-FTD group). Inclusion criterion not met/uncertain: I6 (the full text provided does not present between-group contrast coordinates in a defined stereotactic space [MNI/Talairach] in the main text; coordinates may be in supplemental files not shown here). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded due to E7 (bvFTD group not isolated from concurrent neurological disease).

Exclusion E6 applies: while the study includes VBM-style gray matter density and resting-state fMRI (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=23) and controls (n=35) meeting minimum sample size (I4, I5), the manuscript presents multiparametric classification results (AUCs, selected regional features) rather than reporting at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to controls. I6 and I7 are not met because no voxelwise group contrast coordinates or clear whole-brain statistical maps (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD vs controls are reported in the provided full text. Therefore the paper should be excluded under E6.

Although the study uses VBM (methods describe VBM processing) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and controls (n=14) meeting sample-size requirements, the reported imaging results are ROI-based (hippocampus and posterior cingulate) and the paper does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level coordinates or MNI/Talairach-space between-group contrast results for bvFTD versus controls. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results (I6/I7) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: E6.

Excluded because the study reports VBM-derived regional/ROI measures extracted from a priori masks rather than reporting any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts with stereotactic coordinates. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only ROI/mask-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (sample sizes exceed 6 in patient and control groups). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast in MNI/Talairach space for bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results clearly reported). Full text appears complete.

However, it does NOT include clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease patients (I4 not met). The VBM analysis reported is a group-level whole-brain analysis, but it was performed on controls and AD patients only (25 NC, 7 AD); SV-PPA patients were excluded from the VBM analysis. Therefore there are no between-group contrasts or whole-brain voxelwise results comparing a bvFTD/Pick’s group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the review list apply. Because the paper does not include the target patient population (bvFTD/Pick’s) and provides no bvFTD whole-brain contrasts, it must be excluded.

Inclusion criteria met: I3 — the study used voxelwise gray-matter analyses with SPM2 (a VBM-style, whole-brain approach). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 — the sample is a mixed/pathologically defined FTD spectrum (tau-positive, tau-negative, fv-AD) and does not specifically report a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease group; I5 — the imaging subgroup is small (total n=12: tau-positive n=5; tau-negative n=4; fv-AD n=3), so patient-group sizes for the imaging results are <6; I6 — the reported between-group contrasts are pathology-defined groups vs controls, not a bvFTD vs control contrast (bvFTD group is not isolated); I7 — although whole-brain voxelwise results are reported, they are not identified as coming from a clinically defined bvFTD sample. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are clearly met. Full text appears complete.

Full text is a complete empirical MRI volumetry study of basal forebrain in FTD. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports region-of-interest/volumetric analyses with no whole-brain, voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (patient and control groups both >6 participants). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (does NOT use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; it uses T1 volumetric segmentation/GIF), I6 (no reported between-group contrast results in a defined stereotactic space [MNI/Talairach] comparing bvFTD voxelwise to controls), and I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results). Because E6 is met and key inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a longitudinal volumetric MRI study using semi-automated whole-brain and ventricular atrophy measures (BBSI, VBSI), not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET. Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (11 bvFTD) and sufficient sample sizes with controls, the paper does not report any voxelwise, whole-brain group-level results in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables comparing bvFTD to controls. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria requiring modality (I3) and voxelwise whole-brain results (I6, I7). No exclusion criteria from the list are directly met.

This study uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain voxelwise correlational results across genetic FTD mutation groups, but it does not include or specifically report results from a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group compared directly against healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used) and I5 (patient group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not explicitly present a clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease patient group), I6 (no between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Therefore the article does not satisfy the review’s requirement to provide bvFTD vs. control voxelwise between-group contrasts and must be excluded.

The study uses VBM and includes sufficient sample sizes, but it does not specifically report results for clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) distinct from other FTD variants, nor does it present a clear between-group voxelwise contrast of bvFTD versus controls unpooled with other patient groups. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I4, I6 and I7.

The full text reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (VBM and TBSS aligned to MNI space) comparing a clinical bvFTD group to controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=13), I5 (patient group n≥6 and control group n≥6; HCbvFTD n=25), I6 (reports between-group contrasts in MNI-standard space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results for the bvFTD group), and I8 (results shown in figures/supplementary and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply: this is an original empirical study (not a review), it contains whole-brain voxelwise results (not ROI-only), and although it includes DTI measures, it also includes VBM (an allowed modality). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis objective.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements of the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (bvFTD patient group size in the cohort exceeds 6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET analyses — only structural MRI described), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results provided), I8 (no coordinate tables/figures of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) appear to apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper cannot be included in this coordinate-based whole-brain imaging meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not provide the required bvFTD-specific, whole-brain voxelwise between-group results in standard space. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses 18F-FDG PET imaging) and I5 (FTD patient group size = 36, ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (paper reports FTD patients but does not present results specifically for clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD / Pick’s disease as a distinct target group), I6 (no clearly reported between-group contrast in MNI or Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), and I7 (no clearly presented whole-brain group-level voxelwise coordinates/maps attributable to a bvFTD vs control contrast in the main text; supplemental material not provided here). No exclusion criteria from E5–E9 are directly triggered based on the available full text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging- and analysis-specific inclusion criteria required for the meta-analysis. It used structural MRI distance measures (FA index and frontal atrophy percentages) rather than VBM, fMRI (resting/task), or FDG-PET (I3 not met). It does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results nor stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) from between-group contrasts (I6 and I7 not met). The sample does meet the minimum size requirement (41 patients, 121 comparison subjects; I5 met), but the paper does not explicitly specify behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease as the target diagnostic subgroup (I4 not clearly met). Because the manuscript reports region-based measures/indices without whole-brain voxelwise results, it falls under exclusion E6 (ROI/region-only analyses with no whole-brain results).

This study uses whole-brain VBM and reports group-wise voxelwise neuroimaging results for a C9ORF72 mutation FTLD group (n=11) versus controls, but it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain contrast specifically comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) patient group to healthy controls. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (uses VBM), I5 (patient group n=11 and controls n=15, both ≥6). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (the analyzed patient group is defined by C9ORF72 mutation and is heterogeneous in clinical syndrome rather than a clinically defined bvFTD/Pick’s group), I6 (no between-group contrast reported that specifically compares a bvFTD-only group to controls), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results are not explicitly reported as coming from a bvFTD target sample). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

This study is a retrospective clinical case series that used 18F-FDG PET (with/without 11C-PIB) and included clinically diagnosed FTD patients (behavioral variant criteria applied) with n=7, so it satisfies I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (bvFTD included), and I5 (patient group size ≥6). However, it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach), nor does it provide group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables. Therefore it fails I6 and I7 and does not provide the required whole-brain statistical data for inclusion in the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are directly met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed FTD cases (including behavioral-variant descriptions), but it does not meet the meta-analysis requirements. The paper reports expert visual reads and diagnostic concordance metrics; it does not present any voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses in a stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls, nor does it provide coordinate tables or between-group statistical contrasts. Subgroup counts for bvFTD are not clearly reported, so the required sample-size criterion for the target patient group cannot be verified. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5 (insufficient/unclear patient-group counts), I6 (no between-group stereotactic contrasts), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results), and I8 (no coordinate/voxelwise results in text/tables). Included criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed FTD/bvFTD). No exclusion criteria from the list clearly apply. Full text appears complete for assessment.

This study uses T1-weighted hippocampal subfield volumetry (automated FreeSurfer/GIF segmentation), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET, so it does not meet modality requirement (I3). It reports regional (hippocampal subfield) volume comparisons rather than voxelwise whole‑brain results and provides no stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinates or group-level voxelwise maps, so it fails I6 and I7. The paper does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (counts reported) and meets the sample size requirement (I4 and I5). Because the analyses are region‑of‑interest (hippocampal subfields) with no whole‑brain voxelwise results, exclusion criterion E6 (ROI‑only analyses with no whole‑brain results) applies. Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDE.

The study is excluded because it does not include a clinically diagnosed behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) or Pick's disease group (I4 not met). Although it reports whole-brain VBM analyses of pathology-confirmed groups (FTLD-tau, TDP43A/C), the groups are defined by post-mortem pathology rather than a clinical bvFTD (or Pick) diagnostic group, and no between-group contrast is reported that specifically compares a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls in standard stereotactic space (I6 and I7 not met). The paper does satisfy imaging modality and sample size criteria (I3: VBM used; I5: patient groups have ≥6 subjects), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results for pathology groups, but these do not correspond to the target clinical diagnosis required by the review. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

While the study includes FDG-PET imaging (I3), clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (11 bvFTD patients; I4), and sufficient group sizes (bvFTD n=11; controls n=13; I5), it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTD group to controls. The FDG-PET analysis was single-subject (each patient compared to a healthy control group) and correlations of exosomal HSP70 with the number of hypometabolic voxels were reported, but no group-level voxelwise results or coordinates are provided for the bvFTD group as a whole. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Excluded on the basis of missing required group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I6, I7 not met).

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses voxelwise T1-weighted MRI morphometry/WBGM, VBM-like processing with SPM12/DARTEL), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients per consensus criteria), I5 (FTD group N=39, >6), I7 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise information in the form of 3D SVM weight maps), and I8 (whole-brain maps are presented as figures/slices). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 — the paper does not report at least one between-group contrast comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in a defined stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach). Instead, comparisons are between patient groups (FTD vs AD subtypes or depression) and the reported maps are SVM-derived weight maps rather than mass-univariate between-group coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) volumetric analyses of cerebellar subregions using atlas segmentation and does not present voxel-based whole-brain (VBM), fMRI, or FDG-PET results. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants within genetic groups) and I5 (patient groups and controls each have ≥6 participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; it uses T1 volumetric ROI segmentation), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to controls), and I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting criteria required by the review. It uses structural MRI with region-based parcellation (SABRE) and multivariate partial least squares on regional volumes rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The analyses are region-of-interest/parcellation-based and do not report whole-brain voxelwise group-level coordinates in standard stereotaxic space, nor between-group voxelwise contrasts for an unpooled bvFTD group (I6 and I7 not met). Inclusion criteria that are met: the sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (per Neary criteria) and subgroup size meets the minimum (FTD n=8) with adequate control numbers (I4, I5 met). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (ROI-only analyses without whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3 met) and included sufficient participant numbers (at least 6 patients and controls; I5 met). However, it does not meet key review requirements: participants are genetic FTD mutation carriers (symptomatic and presymptomatic) but the paper does not report a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) group specifically (I4 NOT met). The paper does not report a between-group, voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD patient group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 NOT met), nor does it provide a whole-brain group-level voxelwise result attributable to a bvFTD sample (I7 NOT met). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded.

The study uses whole-brain VBM and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) and adequate control samples, but it does not report any voxelwise, between-group contrast that specifically compares a bvFTD-only group to healthy controls in stereotactic space. Instead, VBM analyses are reported for behavioral subgroups defined by storytelling characteristics (mixed diagnostic composition). Thus key inclusion criteria for this review are not met: no bvFTD-specific whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group results are provided. Exclusion criteria: none met.

This study used T1 MRI with voxelwise processing (W-score maps) and then aggregated into regional (ROI) atrophy burdens, so imaging method meets I3. Sample sizes for patient and control groups exceed 6, so I5 is met. However, the paper does not specifically report results from clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease patients (participants are familial FTLD mutation carriers with heterogeneous clinical syndromes), so I4 is not met. The manuscript does not present whole-brain, group-level voxelwise between-group contrasts (in MNI/Talairach coordinates) comparing a bvFTD group to controls; results are reported as ROI-integrated scores and classifier weights rather than voxelwise coordinate tables/figures, so I6 and I7 are not met. Because only ROI-level results (integrated W-scores/region weights) are reported with no clear whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts, exclusion criterion E6 applies. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Although it uses an eligible imaging modality (FDG-PET; I3) and includes an FTLD patient subgroup with more than six patients (I5), it does not clearly report clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease as required (I4 not met). The FTLD label in this paper is broad and the paper does not state that participants were diagnosed specifically with bvFTD. Critically, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast (bvFTD vs healthy controls) in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) with coordinates; instead analyses focus on diagnostic classification (FDG SPM single-subject comparisons to a normative database) and between-dementia-group logistic/regression results (FTLD vs non-FTLD) without providing whole-brain group-level coordinate results for a bvFTD group (I6 and I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list are directly triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded for failing to meet I4, I6 and I7.

The study is excluded because, although it uses VBM (I3) and has adequate group sizes (converters n=8; controls n≥35) satisfying I5, it does not provide group-level whole-brain voxelwise results specifically for a clinically diagnosed bvFTD-only patient group. The ‘converter’ group is pooled (includes both bvFTD and nfvPPA cases) and the reported voxelwise contrasts compare this pooled converter group to controls, so the paper does not meet: I4 (bvFTD-only sample), I6 (between-group contrast of bvFTD group vs controls without pooling), and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text is complete.

The study used FDG-PET (I3) and included >6 FTD patients and >6 controls (I5). The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD subtypes, including behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) (I4). However, it does NOT report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD-only group to healthy controls (I6 not met). The reported PET result is a voxelwise correlation of metabolic rate with prosocial sexual behavior across combined patient groups (FTD and CBS), not a bvFTD vs control group-level contrast, and no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result is clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only group (I7 not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

This full text meets all required inclusion criteria: (I3) the study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for imaging analyses; (I4) it included a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) group (n=20); (I5) group sizes meet sample thresholds (bvFTD=20; controls=20); (I6) the paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts and states that maximum coordinates are reported in MNI space (i.e., results are presented in a defined stereotactic space) and bvFTD results are not pooled with other patient groups; (I7) whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are described and used in voxel-based morphometry analyses; (I8) results/coordinates are reported and described (including overlap analyses). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is therefore complete for screening purposes. No exclusion criteria were met.

This is an empirical MRI study of white matter hyperintensities using automated segmentation on T1/T2 images in genetic FTD cohorts. It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The paper reports mutation-defined symptomatic FTD groups but does not specify that participants are clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease (I4 not met). Results are reported as regional/zonal volumetric comparisons and summary plots rather than voxelwise, stereotactically-localized (MNI/Talairach) whole-brain coordinates; no voxelwise group-level coordinates are provided (I6 and I7 not met). The study does meet the sample size requirement (I5 met: patient and control groups ≥6). Because the analyses are region-based/zonal (no whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results), this falls under exclusion E6 (only ROI/region-based analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study of bvFTD using structural T1 MRI visual atrophy ratings and survival analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (n=31 patients ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — uses visual structural MRI ratings), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study does not report whole-brain voxelwise results; only region-like/visual rating measures). Therefore the study does not provide the required voxelwise whole-brain imaging results in the specified modalities and must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not provide voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD (or Pick's disease) to controls, and thus does not meet key inclusion criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (no whole-brain voxelwise results; analyses are clinical/visual and PALZ-based rather than reported voxelwise coordinates). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET), I5 (FTD patient group n=18 ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (sample is reported as ‘FTD’ but not specified as behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result reported). Full text appears complete.

Study uses VBM and includes bvFTD patients (11 bvFTD) with adequate sample sizes and reports voxelwise MNI coordinates for associations; however it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group alone to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. VBM analyses were performed as correlations within the combined FTLD patient cohort (and significant inference was made using small-volume correction within pre-specified ROIs). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4 and I5 are met, but I6 and I7 (require a between-group contrast in stereotactic space for the bvFTD group and at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample) are not met. Additionally, the reported neuroimaging inference relied on small-volume/ROI correction rather than whole-brain group-level results, invoking exclusion criterion E6. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded.

Although the study uses VBM (I3) and includes pathologically and clinically characterized FTD cases including Pick disease (PiD) and many clinically diagnosed frontal-variant (fvFTD) cases (satisfying I4) and has sufficient group sizes overall and for PiD and controls (I5), it does NOT report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast specifically comparing a clinically defined behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD/fvFTD) group to controls (I6 not met). The VBM results are reported for pathologic subgroups (FTD-U, PiD, tau exon 10+16) rather than for a clinical bvFTD group, so the required whole-brain, between-group coordinates/results for bvFTD are not available (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded for the review focused on bvFTD whole-brain contrasts.

Full text shows this is an empirical VBM study enrolling bvFTD patients (7) and healthy controls (21), and reports whole-brain VBM and DTI results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD patients included), I5 (patient and control groups ≥6). However, the paper does not report a voxelwise between-group contrast comparing bvFTD patients directly to controls in MNI/Talairach space, nor does it report whole-brain group-level voxelwise results that are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group alone (results are correlational across participants and conjunctions across measures). Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5,E6,E7,E8,E9) appear to apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and analysis inclusion criteria. Exclusion ID met: E6 (study reports only region-based/ROI volumetric analyses focused on frontal lobes and does not present whole-brain, voxelwise results). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; n=18) and I5 (bvFTD group size ≥6). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural T1-weighted MRI volumetry with multi-atlas regional segmentation, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast reported comparing bvFTD to healthy controls in standard stereotactic space; comparisons are between patient groups), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the paper does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

This full-text reports an empirical resting-state fMRI study (with VBM structural analysis) comparing clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD (n=25) to controls (n=29) and AD (n=31). It uses voxel-wise, whole-brain analyses (dual regression and voxel-wise permutation testing) with results presented in MNI-152 space and FWE-corrected TFCE statistics, and describes voxelwise group-level contrasts (bvFTD vs controls and bvFTD vs AD). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. The paper provides whole-brain voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, seed-only, DTI-only, comorbid psychiatric sample issues) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This empirical study used Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (and TBSS/DTI) as imaging modalities and explicitly included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=10) and healthy controls (n=26). The bvFTD patient group meets the minimum sample size requirement (>=6) and controls also exceed the minimum (>=6). The paper reports that separate VBM group-level analyses were run for each patient group (including bvFTD) versus healthy controls and refers to results/coordinates reported in the Supplementary Information (S11), satisfying the requirement for at least one between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast in stereotactic space. Whole-brain VBM and TBSS results (with cluster/peak reporting and FWE-corrected thresholds) are described in the text and figures, and the authors note coordinates/peaks and use standard MNI space. Supplementary materials are acceptable per inclusion rules. Given these points, the study meets all specified inclusion criteria for the bvFTD meta-analysis. Confidence is somewhat reduced because some between-group coordinate tables are reported in Supplementary Information rather than the main text, but the manuscript clearly indicates those whole-brain contrasts were performed and reported.

This study is excluded because it reports primarily ROI- and summary-index-based imaging results and does not present whole-brain, voxelwise group-level coordinate results required for inclusion. Exclusion ID met: E6 (reports only ROI/summary analyses with no clear whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (uses FDG-PET and VBM-derived indices). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (unclear whether the FTD sample is specifically behavioral variant FTD or Pick's disease — the paper reports FTD broadly and mentions subtypes but does not specify bvFTD cases), I5 (FTD subgroup size is not provided in the provided text — cannot verify >=6 patients in the bvFTD/Pick's group), I6 (no reported between-group contrasts in stereotactic space specifically comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results identified). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete: false).

This is an empirical FDG-PET study that specifically investigates bvFTD. It includes clinically and pathologically diagnosed bvFTD participants (Center-A and Center-B) with patient group sizes well above 6 and multiple healthy control groups (n≥6). The imaging data were normalized to MNI space and analyzed voxelwise using spatial covariance/PCA yielding whole-brain topographies (bFDRP) reported and visualized; group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are explicitly described and attributed to the bvFTD group. Results are presented in figures and described in MNI-normalized space; bootstrap/voxelwise statistics and thresholds are reported. The paper is original empirical research (not a review), does not rely solely on ROI analyses, and does not fall under excluded modalities. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on whole-brain T1-weighted MRI and reports voxelwise group comparisons with MNI coordinates. The ALS-FTD subgroup (n=18) met clinical Neary criteria for FTD and predominantly showed behavioral abnormalities consistent with bvFTD; neurologic disease controls (n=15) are included. VBM whole-brain results (voxelwise, corrected p<0.05) are reported for ALS-FTD versus controls and versus other ALS subgroups and coordinate tables (MNI) are provided. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patient and control groups ≥6). The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present; supplementary material being online is acceptable. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=18) and uses 18F-FDG PET (I4, I3) with at least 6 patients in the bvFTD group (I5). It reports voxel-wise, whole-brain PET analyses relating metabolism to oculomotor parameters (results depicted in figures and described in text) (I8). However, it does not present any between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The FDG-PET results are correlational analyses across a combined patient set (n=18) and the controls do not appear to have FDG-PET data for group comparison; no bvFTD vs. control voxelwise contrast or coordinate table is reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met, so the study must be excluded.

This is a resting-state fMRI study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, but it does not provide voxelwise whole-brain (MNI/Talairach) between-group contrasts for a bvFTD-only group. The bvFTD-only subgroup has N=3 (<6), and bvFTD patients are pooled with ALS-FTD in subgroup analyses (bvFTD+ n=9), so there is no unpooled bvFTD vs. control voxelwise result. Analyses are ROI/parcellation-based graph/network metrics (82 VOIs) and edge/hub results rather than whole-brain voxelwise coordinates, so it meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only/no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI modality) and I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (bvFTD patient group <6 for bvFTD-only), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD-only to controls), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level result in stereotactic space). Full text appears complete.

This study meets several inclusion criteria for the review: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients consistent with behavioral-variant FTD), I5 (sufficient sample sizes: FTD n=30; controls n=20), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results identified for the FTD subgroup in diagnostic subgroup interaction analyses), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/figures). However, it fails to meet I6: the paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast in standard (MNI/Talairach) space directly comparing the bvFTD/FTD group to healthy controls (the authors explicitly state that normal controls were not used for any VBM analysis). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded because it lacks the required bvFTD vs control whole-brain between-group contrast (I6 not met).

Although this empirical study used whole-brain VBM (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=10) within the cohort (I4) and met minimum group sizes (patients and healthy controls; I5), it does NOT present a between-group voxelwise contrast directly comparing the bvFTD subgroup to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) (fails I6). The VBM results reported are primarily correlational analyses within the pooled FTLD group and a pooled FTLD vs control atrophy map; subgroup analyses are mentioned but no bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain coordinate results or tables are provided/identified (fails I7/I6). Therefore it does not provide the required between-group whole-brain result for bvFTD unpooled from other syndromic groups and must be excluded.

While this paper uses whole-brain structural MRI with voxelwise gray-matter maps (VBM-like) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=41) and adequate control sample (n=56), it does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD patients to controls as a distinct group-level result. The analyses focus on multivariate correlations (SCCAN) between PBAC subscales and gray matter across a mixed cohort of controls and multiple patient phenotypes, rather than providing bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I5 are met, but I6 and I7 (requiring at least one between-group bvFTD vs control contrast reported in a standard stereotactic space and a group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group) are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (SPM99 VBM) and includes a behavioral-variant-like subgroup (SOC/EXEC), with sufficient sample sizes (FTD-related n=73; controls n=13). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (voxelwise correlations of CSF tau with gray matter atrophy) in the FTD patient group. However, it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrast in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) directly comparing a bvFTD (SOC/EXEC) group to healthy controls where the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups. Inclusion criterion I6 (a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls) is therefore not met. Accordingly, the study must be excluded.

This study uses VBM and includes a clinically-diagnosed FTD subgroup with adequate sample size, but it does not report any between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts directly comparing the bvFTD/FTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. The VBM analyses are covariate-based regressions across a pooled sample (patients and controls) relating gray matter volume to music-task performance; results are presented as correlations with task scores rather than as group-level FTD vs control contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (explicit between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD to controls; at least one group-level whole-brain result from the target sample) are not met. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed FTD with behavioral features consistent with bvFTD), I5 (patient and control group sizes meet the >=6 threshold). No exclusion criteria apply. Consequently the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study is empirical and includes 29 clinically diagnosed FTD patients (meets I4 and I5). However, it does not meet key imaging and analysis requirements for the review: the imaging reported are SPECT and PET by visual inspection with quadrant laterality categorizations rather than an explicit use of VBM, fMRI, or specified FDG-PET with voxelwise analyses (I3 not met). Crucially, no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) with coordinate reporting are provided (I6 and I7 not met). Thus it falls under exclusion E6 (no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses VBM (I3) and includes an adequate sample size (18 patients, 17 controls) satisfying I5. The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD cases with frontal-variant/behavioural features (fvFTD), so participants with behavioural-variant presentations are present (I4). However, the paper does not report a between-group whole-brain contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD (or fvFTD-only) group to controls that is not pooled with other FTD subtypes. The group-level VBM contrast reported is for a heterogeneous FTD group versus controls, and the behavioural analysis is a covariate correlation (NPI) across the mixed FTD cohort rather than a bvFTD-only voxelwise group contrast. Therefore criteria I6 and I7 are not met (no isolated bvFTD group whole-brain between-group result). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Exclusion is based on failing required inclusion criteria I6 and I7.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging- and analysis-related inclusion criteria required for the review and reports only region-of-interest volumetry. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (sample size ≥6 participants in patient group; 21 FTD patients, with 21 controls).
