(c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural MRI volumetry, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I4 (participants are described as FTD but not specified as behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast reported in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study is excluded because although it uses whole-brain VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTLD patients (7/10; counted as bvFTD-like cases) (I4), and has sufficient group sizes (patients and controls ≥6) (I5), it does NOT provide a bvFTD-only group-level contrast or coordinates specific to a bvFTD sample. The ALS/FTLD patient group is heterogeneous (includes 7 frontal-variant, 2 semantic dementia, 1 PNFA) and is comorbid with ALS, so the reported ALS/FTLD vs control VBM results pool different FTLD variants and include concurrent neurological disease. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (a between-group contrast and clear whole-brain voxelwise result specific to a bvFTD group) are not met. Additionally, the sample includes comorbid neurological disease (ALS), triggering exclusion criterion E7. Full article text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because it does not report a between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group unpooled from other FTD subtypes to healthy controls (inclusion criterion I6 not met). It also does not present whole-brain results clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target sample (I7 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically characterized behavioral-presentation FTD patients consistent with bvFTD; 48/62), and I5 (patient N=62 and controls N=14, both ≥6). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because the meta-analysis requires bvFTD-specific between-group voxelwise contrasts, this mixed-sample FTD VBM study is not eligible.

This article is a narrative review of imaging in dementia (MRI, FDG-PET, fMRI, VBM are discussed) and does not report original empirical data from a patient sample. It does not include an original patient cohort of clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease with ≥6 patients, nor does it report any between-group whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach space from a bvFTD sample. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E8 (non-empirical paper) and does not satisfy required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not empirically use VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET in an original sample), I4 (no original bvFTD/Pick’s sample), I5 (no patient/control sample sizes reported as empirical groups ≥6), I6 (no between-group contrast in stereotactic space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from target sample), I8 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported). Full text appears to be a complete narrative review rather than an original empirical article; fulltext_incomplete set to false.

Excluded because imaging modality is SPECT rather than VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET, and the paper does not report whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts in stereotactic space vs. controls. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed behavioural FTD sample), I5 (sample size n=74 ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality mismatch — SPECT), I6 (no between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach coordinates comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only region-based/quadrant SPECT ratings and no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text appears to be a narrative review or non-empirical article and the provided content is incomplete (only references). Exclusion criteria met: E8 (non-empirical paper without original data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET methods reported in primary data), I4 (no clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease patient sample), I5 (no sample size ≥6 patients reported), I6 (no between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach coordinates), I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results), I8 (no coordinates/figures of whole-brain results). Because core sections (methods, results) are missing, fulltext_incomplete=true.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=50) and uses VBM as one of its MRI quantification methods, it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrast results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach) comparing the bvFTD group to controls. The paper reports classification performance (DSI sensitivities) based on VBM-derived features, but no voxelwise statistical maps, coordinate tables, or whole-brain group contrasts are provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (and the reporting form requirement I8) are not met. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7, I8. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) explicitly apply; exclusion arises from failure to meet required inclusion criteria.

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing a subgroup of FTD patients with prominent social/executive disorder (SOC/EXEC), corresponding to behavioral-variant FTD, to healthy controls. It uses whole-brain VBM in SPM99 with group-level two-sample t tests and regression analyses, reporting voxelwise atrophy and neuroanatomical clusters (BA labels, p-values) in the SOC/EXEC group and a regression of behavior onto gray matter. Sample sizes meet minimums (SOC/EXEC n=12; controls n=12). The paper provides full methods, results, and figures indicating whole-brain voxelwise findings derived from normalized brains (standardized brain coordinates in SPM), and reports group-level contrasts specific to the SOC/EXEC group. Therefore inclusion criteria for imaging modality (I3), target sample (I4), sample size (I5), reporting of between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard space (I6), and whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I7) are satisfied; whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables (I8). Full text appears complete.

Although this study used whole-brain VBM (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within its sample (I4), had adequate group sizes (≥6 patients and controls) (I5), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I7) presented in figures/tables (I8), it does NOT provide a between-group contrast that compares a bvFTD-only group to controls without pooling bvFTD with other clinical variants. The reported contrasts are PGRN(+) vs controls and PGRN(−) vs controls, each of which include mixed clinical phenotypes (bvFTD, SD, CBS). Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not met, and the study cannot be included for a meta-analysis requiring bvFTD-specific between-group coordinates. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate bvFTD patients and does not use an eligible imaging modality. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports ROI-based structural MRI volumes from FreeSurfer with no voxelwise/whole-brain VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET results). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; used ROI structural volumes), I4 (sample consists of mild Alzheimer’s disease patients, not clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease), I5 (no bvFTD patient group of ≥6 participants), I6 (no between-group voxelwise MNI/Talairach contrast comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from a bvFTD sample), I8 (no coordinate tables/voxelwise results for bvFTD). No inclusion criteria were satisfied.

Excluded because the study uses surface-based morphometry (cortical thickness and fractal dimension) rather than one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), triggering exclusion criterion E9. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD patients included; 8 bvFTD cases diagnosed by consensus criteria) and I5 (bvFTD subgroup n=8 >=6; controls n=28 >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality mismatch — not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no explicit between-group contrast reported in a standard stereotactic coordinate space [MNI/Talairach] for bvFTD vs controls), and I7 (no clearly reported whole-brain voxelwise coordinate-based result in stereotactic space for the bvFTD target group). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded from this review.

This study uses VBM (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) with adequate control groups (>=6) (I4, I5). The paper reports between-group contrasts comparing the bvFTD group to controls within SPM/VBM frameworks normalized to MNI space and reports ROI-based correlations (I6). However, the bvFTD-versus-controls results are presented as ROI/small-volume-corrected analyses (region-of-interest SVC) rather than as group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) results clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample. Thus it does not provide a whole-brain, voxelwise result for the target bvFTD group (I7 not met). Because the bvFTD results are only ROI/SVC and there is no bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise contrast, this meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only reporting with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study is excluded.

This study uses FDG-PET and includes a clinically diagnosed FTD subgroup (n=9) within an FTLD sample of 14 patients, and provides whole-brain voxelwise SPM results in stereotaxic space. However, it does NOT report a between-group contrast of bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) versus healthy controls, and the reported whole-brain results are for a pooled FTLD group (FTD, SD, PPA) compared to an EOAD patient group rather than isolated bvFTD vs controls. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study used FDG-PET (I3) and includes sufficient sample sizes (FTD n=14; controls n=33) meeting I5. However, it does not provide a clear between-group, whole-brain, voxelwise contrast in standard stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls: group-level voxelwise coordinate tables or coordinates are not reported, and the analyses focus on individual SSP comparisons and diagnostic accuracy rather than group-level voxelwise contrasts. In addition, the FTD sample was defined pathologically and was not prospectively or uniformly clinically classified as behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD); clinical subtyping was retrospective and some cases were difficult to classify, so I4 is not clearly satisfied. Therefore the study fails to meet I6 and I7 (and I4 is not clearly met) and cannot be included.

Excluded because the study does not meet key imaging and analytic inclusion criteria required by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (the paper reports two patients who fulfilled possible bvFTD criteria). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET reported — only structural MRI and DaTSCAN), I5 (patient group size <6 — only 2 bvFTD cases), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) were triggered. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 — the study reports hippocampal volumetry and visual rating (ROI-based) with no whole-brain voxelwise results. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 — includes a clinical FTD subgroup (frontotemporal dementia, i.e., behavioral variant FTD) and I5 — sample size for FTLD patients is 42 (≥6) and controls present. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 — imaging modality is structural MRI volumetry/MTA rating, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; I6 — no reported between-group contrast coordinates in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls; I7 — no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results for the target sample. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails the modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements necessary for inclusion.

This study does not meet key imaging and analysis criteria for inclusion. While it includes an adequate FTD patient sample (15 FTD patients; I5 satisfied), the imaging modality/analysis is automated volumetric segmentation and regional volume (hippocampal and lobar volumes) rather than Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM), fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The paper reports regional/ROI volumetric results and percentiles, but does not present whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls; thus I6 and I7 are not met. Furthermore, the FTD subtype is not specified as behavioral-variant (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not confirmed). Exclusion criterion E6 applies because only ROI/volumetric (non–whole-brain voxelwise) results are reported. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Excluded because the study does not clearly meet the review’s target-sample requirement for bvFTD and does not report the required patient-vs-control whole-brain contrasts for bvFTD. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM) and I5 (patient group n=8 and control group n=26, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (paper does not explicitly state participants have clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD; it only says FTD/type without specifying bvFTD), I6 (no clear between-group contrast reported that compares a bvFTD-only group to controls in MNI/Talairach space — reported contrasts are carrier vs non-carrier within FTD and within AD), and I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD vs control comparison). Exclusion criteria met: none (no applicable exclusion IDs). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses VBM preprocessing (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=55) (I4), and has adequate patient and control group sizes (I5). However, the paper does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate tables in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls; analyses are based on a priori ROI volumetric extractions and machine-learning classification. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. Exclusion criterion E6 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study does not use the required imaging modalities (it uses FreeSurfer regional volumetry and cortical thickness, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — violates I3), does not specifically include clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD or Pick's disease (FTD group is general, not clearly bvFTD — violates I4), and does not report whole-brain voxelwise, coordinate-based contrasts in standard (MNI/Talairach) space comparing a bvFTD group to controls (violates I6 and I7). Inclusion criterion I5 is met (FTD patient group n=22 >6). Exclusion criteria E6 and E9 apply because the paper reports only ROI/cortical-thickness analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results and does not use acceptable modalities. Full text appears complete.

The study used FDG-PET and SPM5 and included an FTD patient group (n=7) with healthy controls (n=18), so imaging modality (I3) and sample size (I5) criteria are met. However, the paper reports results for a general FTD group without specifying behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease; inclusion criterion I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease) is not satisfied. Consequently, criteria that require bvFTD-specific between-group voxelwise contrasts and whole-brain results (I6, I7, I8) are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not specifically report on bvFTD/Pick’s disease patients.

Excluded because study does not meet key imaging and analysis inclusion criteria. Although it includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (meets I4) and has sufficient patient sample size (72; meets I5), it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met), reports no between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls (I6 not met), and provides no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I7 not met). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) directly apply, but failure to meet the above inclusion criteria mandates exclusion.

This is an empirical study of sleep/activity (actigraphy and sleep diaries) in bvFTD patients—not an imaging study. Inclusion met: I4 (subjects are clinically diagnosed bvFTD) and I5 (patient group n=13; control groups ≥6). Inclusion not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast in MNI/Talairach space), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the paper does not meet all required imaging/whole-brain outcome criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical multicenter 18F-FDG PET study that includes a frontal-variant FTD group (frontal variant = behavioral variant FTD), with 98 FTD patients and 110 controls (meets sample size criterion). Scans were spatially normalized to the Talairach atlas and analyzed voxelwise (Neurostat, 3D-SSP maps, voxelwise Z scores), producing group-level whole-brain results comparing FTD (frontal variant) to controls and to other dementia groups. Results for the FTD group are reported separately (not pooled) and presented as voxelwise/whole-brain maps and group comparisons. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies imaging modality (FDG-PET), diagnostic group (frontal/bvFTD), sufficient sample size, and reports whole-brain Talairach-space voxelwise group results for bvFTD vs controls.

This is a case series of a PGRN-mutation family using structural MRI (qualitative) and neuropathology, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none of the explicit exclusion criteria (E5-E9) strictly apply. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (participants included clinically diagnosed FTD cases, including behavioral presentations). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I3 (imaging modality is structural MRI, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I5 (imaging/neuroimaging sample with analyzable data is <6 participants for the modalities required), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach coordinates comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and is excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key bvFTD-specific inclusion criteria. Although it uses VBM (I3 satisfied) and has adequate group sizes (FTD n=9, controls n=10; I5 satisfied), it does not include a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease group explicitly (I4 not met). The VBM analysis was a covariate-only correlation across all diagnostic groups rather than a between-group, voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met) and therefore does not provide whole-brain group-level results from a target bvFTD sample (I7 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (7 participants) (I4) with a healthy control group (40) (I5); reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in MNI space for individual phenotypes (including bvFTD vs controls) (I6, I7) and presents results in figures/text (I8). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met.

The study is excluded because it does not use an acceptable imaging modality (I3 not met) and does not report any coordinate-based, voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrasts (I6 and I7 not met). It uses conventional structural MRI visual/region ratings (exemplar-based atrophy scores across 12 areas) rather than VBM, FDG‑PET, or fMRI, and presents region-level atrophy ratings rather than whole-brain voxelwise results; this meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI/region-only analyses with no whole-brain results). The paper does include clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia cases (meets I4) and has sufficient patient sample size (meets I5), but critical imaging and reporting criteria for inclusion (I3, I6, I7) are not satisfied. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Full text appears incomplete and consists mainly of references; the article appears to be a narrative review rather than an original empirical study. Exclusion IDs met: E5 (systematic reviews/meta-analyses) and E8 (non-empirical review without original data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no evidence the study used VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET as original methods), I4 (no report of clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s patients as an original sample), I5 (no participant counts reported; patient/control groups not described), I6 (no between-group coordinate-based contrasts reported), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results from a target sample), I8 (no qualifying whole-brain results in tables/figures/supplement). Because core article content (methods, results) is missing, fulltext_incomplete=true.

This study used VBM (I3), included a social/dysexecutive (SOC/EXEC) FTLD subgroup consistent with behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) (I4), and the patient (SOC/EXEC n=17) and control (n=12) group sizes meet the sample-size criterion (I5). However, the paper does not report any group-level between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTD/SOC-EXEC group to controls (I6 not met). It also does not present a group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample (I7 not met). The imaging approach is primarily subject-level VBM maps intersected with BA ROIs and subsequent ROI-based analyses, so it effectively lacks reported whole-brain group contrasts and therefore falls under exclusion E6 (ROI-only/no whole-brain group results). Consequently, the study is excluded.

This is a structural MRI study using voxel-wise morphometric analyses (SPM12) reporting voxelwise maps and coordinates in standard space, and has adequate group sizes, but it does NOT target clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease groups or report a between-group contrast of a bvFTD group versus controls. Specifically: (a) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (voxel-wise morphometry/VBM-like analysis), I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6), I8 (coordinates reported in standard space/supplement). (b) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (participants are familial FTLD mutation carriers; the paper does not specify a clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease group), I6 (no between-group contrast reported that compares a bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (while whole-brain voxelwise maps are reported for mutation-stage groups, they are not clearly identified as arising from a bvFTD target sample). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Therefore the paper should be excluded for not meeting the review’s target-sample and contrast requirements.

This study is excluded because it does not meet required imaging and analysis criteria for the meta-analysis. It includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients (consistent with bvFTD; meets I4) and sufficient sample sizes (21 patients and control groups; meets I5). However, it does not use one of the required imaging modalities/analyses (VBM, fMRI, or explicitly FDG-PET) nor does it report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Instead, PET/SPECT data were rated qualitatively/regionally by raters (regional/visual ratings) with no coordinate tables or voxelwise contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 are not met, and exclusion criterion E6 (studies with only ROI/regional analyses and no whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical study that includes FDG-PET and an FTD patient group (n=10), so it meets I3 (FDG-PET) and I5 (≥6 patients). However, the paper does not report any voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts in a stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide coordinate tables/figures; PET data were analyzed via visual consensus reads rather than voxelwise analyses. The full text also does not explicitly state that the FTD subgroup consists of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I4, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (no whole-brain/voxelwise results).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 — the study performs ROI/VOI-based feature extraction using the AAL parcellation and reports machine-learning classification (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity) rather than any group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical contrasts or coordinate tables in MNI/Talairach space. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 — imaging modality is FDG-PET; I5 — sample sizes meet requirement (FTD n=43; controls n=40). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 — the paper reports ‘FTD’ but does not specify behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease specifically; I6 — no between-group voxelwise contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to controls is reported; I7 — no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) result from the target sample is provided. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it lacks whole-brain voxelwise contrasts for a defined bvFTD sample and meets exclusion E6.

This study is excluded because it does not address behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (sample size criterion: the study used >6 images/subjects per group: 43 amyloid-negative and 45 amyloid-positive). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (imaging modality—used 11C-PiB amyloid PET, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I4 (sample does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease patients), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast reported in MNI/Talairach comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results from a bvFTD sample). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the paper does not meet the review’s target population or outcome reporting requirements.

The study uses FDG-PET imaging (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (6 in template creation and 24 in validation) meeting the minimum group size (I4, I5). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for the bvFTD subgroup (second-level SPM analyses and Table 3 coordinates), providing between-group contrasts (derived from single-subject vs control contrasts aggregated at group level) in MNI space, and includes coordinate tables/figures (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not target behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) as required. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (uses FDG-PET imaging). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I4 — the sample does not include a defined bvFTD or Pick’s disease group (cohort comprises mixed diagnoses with only 4 FTLD cases, not specified as bvFTD/Pick’s); I5 — the target patient subgroup (bvFTD/Pick’s) does not have ≥6 participants; I6 — no between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast reported comparing a bvFTD group to controls (bvFTD not isolated or analyzed separately); I7 — no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results reported for a bvFTD target group. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

This study uses 18F-FDG PET (meets I3) but does not meet multiple other inclusion criteria required for a bvFTD meta-analysis. The paper reports a heterogeneous clinical sample of various dementias and only five patients labeled as FTD (not clearly specified as behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease), so I4 is not satisfied and I5 (minimum n=6 for patient group) is not met. No between-group voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls are reported, and no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results or coordinate tables are provided (I6 and I7 not met). The analyses are visual/region-based and categorical (no voxelwise whole-brain results), which triggers exclusion E6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded.

This is an empirical, multimodal imaging study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=39) and healthy controls (n=61), uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses in MNI space, and reports group-level, voxelwise comparisons and coordinates correlating gray matter with behavioral measures. The methods describe whole-brain FSL-VBM processing, voxelwise GLM with permutation testing, and results/figures/tables showing VBM clusters (MNI). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not only DTI/FC/thickness). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study is excluded because it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (it uses manual ROI volumetric MRI measures) and does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed FTD patients; progressive aphasia cases were excluded and the remaining patients were judged to fulfill FTD criteria) and I5 (sample size: 10 FTD patients and 27 controls, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modalities VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach coordinate space), and I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore the paper does not meet the meta-analysis imaging/methodological requirements and is excluded.

This study used FDG-PET (meets I3) and includes patient and control groups >6 participants (meets I5). However it does NOT include clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease patients — participants are probable Alzheimer’s disease, amnestic MCI, and controls (fails I4). The paper does not report whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls and does not provide coordinate tables for such results (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it does not address the review’s target population or report the required whole-brain voxelwise bvFTD vs. control results. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion provided). Exclusion criteria applied: E6 (no whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6, I7.

This is a single-case longitudinal case report of a patient with behavioral-variant FTD using structural MRI volumetry and manual segmentations; it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET at the group level, nor does it report group-level between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard (MNI/Talairach) space. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results; analyses are single-subject/ROI-style). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (patient clinically diagnosed with bvFTD). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET as required), I5 (fewer than 6 participants — only one case), I6 (no between-group contrast coordinates/results), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed FTLD patients with a behavioral-variant subgroup (bvFTD n=10) (I4), and both patient and control groups exceed the minimum size (bvFTD n=10; controls n=112) (I5). However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The SPM work described is single-subject comparisons against a control database and rater-based diagnostic accuracy; no group-level voxelwise results or coordinate tables for the bvFTD group are presented in the provided full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from the target bvFTD group) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the text provided.

This study is excluded because it does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a clinically defined bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) group to controls, and instead reports visual/qualitative FDG- and amyloid-PET reads. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only non-whole‑brain/coordinate results reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG‑PET was used). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no clear sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick's disease specified), I5 (no evidence of ≥6 bvFTD patients or a corresponding control group for bvFTD), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD to controls in standard space), I7 and I8 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results presented). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Although the study used whole-brain voxelwise GM-based methods (VBM-style preprocessing) and included FTLD with a behavioral-variant FTLD subgroup (bvFTD; n=9) and adequate group sizes overall, it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts (with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space) specifically comparing the bvFTD subgroup to controls. The paper focuses on SVM classification accuracy rather than reporting group-level whole-brain statistical results/coordinates for bvFTD versus controls. Therefore it fails to meet I6 (between-group contrast in defined stereotactic space for bvFTD vs controls) and I7 (at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified for the target sample). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not report whole-brain voxelwise (e.g., VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET) group-level results for clinically-diagnosed bvFTD. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study uses ROI/region-wise volumetry and grading features without reporting whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (sample sizes exceed 6 participants per patient and control groups: FTLD n=92, SMC n=118). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, task/resting‑state fMRI, or FDG‑PET — used T1/FLAIR regional volumes and grading), I4 (did not specifically include clinically-diagnosed behavioral variant FTD or Pick’s disease — subjects labeled as FTLD without explicit bvFTD subgrouping), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level result clearly identified for the target sample). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study includes pathologically confirmed FTLD cases (including 9 behavioral-variant FTLD patients) and uses voxel-wise grey-matter segmentation/normalization (SPM, modulation) consistent with VBM methods (I3, I4, I5 met). However, the paper does not report any whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD (or FTLD sub-group) to healthy controls. The analyses focus on SVM classification (AD vs FTLD and AD vs controls) and present SVM weight maps and classification accuracies rather than conventional between-group voxelwise statistical contrasts/coordinate tables for bvFTD vs controls. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (no reported bvFTD vs control voxelwise contrast in stereotactic coordinates). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study does not meet the imaging and whole-brain reporting requirements for this meta-analysis. Exclusion rationale: (E9) The paper reports cortical thickness and region-of-interest/subcortical volume analyses derived from FreeSurfer (cortical thickness/volumetry), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; (E6) it does not report whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables — analyses are ROI/parcel-based. Inclusion criteria met: (I4) includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=54); (I5) patient group size ≥6. Inclusion criteria not met: (I3) imaging modality (VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET) not used; (I6) no between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls in stereotactic space; (I7) no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates. Full text appears complete.

This article is a narrative evidence review/consensus guideline, not an original empirical study. It does not present an independent sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease patients, does not report group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to controls, and does not provide primary imaging data (FDG-PET findings are summarized from other studies). Therefore it fails all required inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criteria for non-empirical/systematic review material. Exclusion IDs met: E5, E8. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (no original imaging modality data reported as primary study), I4 (no bvFTD/Pick’s patient sample reported as original data), I5 (no primary patient/control sample with counts), I6 (no between-group contrasts in stereotactic space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from a target sample), I8 (no qualifying whole-brain results in coordinates/figures from original data). Full text appears complete (review article).

This study used FDG-PET (meets I3) but does not include a patient group of clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease subjects at baseline. Only a small number (4–5) of MCI cases converted to probable bvFTD at follow-up (fewer than the required N>=6), and the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD patient group to controls in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails I4, I5, I6 and I7. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are met.

Although this study uses VBM (I3), includes a clearly defined bvFTD subgroup (n=34) (I4), and has an adequate patient and control sample size (controls n=32) (I5), it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrasts directly comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. The VBM analysis was conducted across the patient cohort to assess symptom-related gray matter associations and appears to include patients only (no patient-versus-control whole-brain group comparison reported). Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (a between-group bvFTD vs control voxelwise contrast reported, and at least one whole-brain group-level voxelwise result for the target sample) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used VBM and included bvFTD patients (N=23) but does not provide any between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls nor report whole-brain voxelwise results that are specifically from a bvFTD vs control contrast. Instead, VBM correlations are reported across a pooled sample of 75 neurodegeneration patients with diagnosis entered as covariates. Thus it fails to meet criteria requiring (I6) a bvFTD-specific between-group contrast and (I7) at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD participants included), I5 (bvFTD group size >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=10) and healthy controls (n=19) meeting sample size requirements (I4, I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM results presented in figures (I7, I8), it does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast (bvFTD vs healthy controls) in a defined stereotactic space for the bvFTD group unpooled with other patient groups. The neuroimaging results are within-group neuroanatomical associations (correlations between gray matter and cardiac reactivity/emotion identification) rather than a direct group-level bvFTD vs control coordinate-based contrast. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not met, and the study must be excluded.

This is a single-case tau PET ([F]AV-1451) study in a MAPT mutation bvFTD patient compared to 12 controls. Inclusion met: I4 (contains a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient). Inclusion NOT met: I3 (imaging modality is tau-PET tracer [F]AV-1451, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I5 (patient group n=1, below required ≥6), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast reported in MNI/Talairach space for a bvFTD group), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result identified for the target sample). Exclusion met: E6 (analyses are region-of-interest/parcellation based with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria and meets an exclusion criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is FAV-1451 PET and structural MRI, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I5 (patient sample size = 1, below required >=6), I6 (no group-level between-group contrast in standard MNI/Talairach space for a bvFTD group — analysis is a single case vs controls using regional parcellation), I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result from a bvFTD group). Exclusion criterion applied: E6 (analysis is ROI/parcellation-based with no qualifying whole-brain group-level voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Given these mismatches the study must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used FDG-PET), I5 (FTD patient group n=10 and healthy control group n=46 meet minimum sample sizes), I7 (voxelwise, whole-brain SPM group-level contrasts are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (the paper does not report between-group contrast results in a defined stereotactic coordinate space such as MNI or Talairach; no coordinate tables or explicit stereotactic coordinates are provided in the full text), I4 (the clinical sample is described as frontotemporal dementia per Lund and Manchester criteria but the paper does not explicitly state 'behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD)' or Pick's disease; vagueness about variant undermines certainty that target diagnosis is bvFTD). No exclusion criteria from the provided list were directly violated. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Given failure to satisfy I6 (and uncertainty about I4), the study must be excluded from the bvFTD meta-analysis.

This study does not meet key inclusion requirements for a bvFTD-focused voxelwise meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM/TBM methods were used) and I5 (FTD group N=87 and controls N=302, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 — the sample comprises a heterogeneous FTD group (behavioral variant, semantic dementia, progressive nonfluent aphasia combined) and the paper does not report results specifically for clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease as a separate target group; I6 — the paper does not present a between-group contrast explicitly comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach); I7 — there are no clearly identified whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results reported for a bvFTD target sample in the main text (appendix referenced but not providing target-specific stereotactic coordinates in the provided full text). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered by the provided content.

The study uses FDG-PET and includes an FTD patient group (n=14) but does not report any whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level contrasts in a standardized coordinate space (MNI/Talairach). Imaging assessment was qualitative/visual rather than VBM/voxelwise analysis; no coordinates or voxelwise statistical maps are provided. Therefore it fails the meta-analysis requirements for whole-brain voxelwise results.

Full text is complete. This study uses deep-learning on raw 3D T1-weighted structural MRI and reports voxelwise "contribution maps" derived from guided backpropagation mapped to MNI space. However, it does NOT use one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET) (I3 not met). The FTD sample is reported generically as FTD (from NIFD) and the paper does not specify clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or report results specifically for a bvFTD subgroup (I4 not met). Although the study includes large patient groups (I5 met) and conducts voxelwise t-tests on contribution maps, it does not report between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard stereotaxic space comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are clearly triggered.

This study uses VBM (I3) and includes sufficiently large patient subgroups and controls (I5). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses for patient subgroups and describes atrophy for the SOC/EXEC (nonaphasic social/executive) subgroup (I7). However, it does not explicitly identify a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) or Pick’s disease group by that label (I4 not clearly satisfied; SOC/EXEC appears to correspond to behavioral presentation but is not explicitly reported as bvFTD). Critically, the paper does not provide a between-group contrast result in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) that is clearly reported for the SOC/EXEC/bvFTD subgroup (I6 not met) — coordinates/tables appear absent for this subgroup. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for inclusion in the bvFTD meta-analysis.

The study is empirical and includes 20 clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patients (I4) with sufficient patient sample size (I5). However, it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET: imaging is volumetric/Surface-based MRI processed with FreeSurfer (global gray matter volume/cortical reconstruction), i.e., cortical thickness/volumetry methods, so it fails I3 and meets exclusion E9. The paper reports no healthy control group or between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls in stereotactic space (no MNI/Talairach coordinates), so it fails I6 and I7. Therefore it does not provide the required whole-brain, voxelwise coordinate results for inclusion and is excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not report a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast specifically for a bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) group unpooled from other FTD variants. Although bvFTD patients are included within the FTSD group (16 bvFTD + 4 PPA), all primary VBM contrasts are reported for the combined FTSD group (bvFTD + PPA) rather than for bvFTD-only vs controls in MNI/Talairach space. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD participants included), I5 (patient and control groups exceed N>=6), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (reporting of results in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported that compares bvFTD-only group to controls without pooling). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete. Given the explicit I6 requirement, the study must be excluded.

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses relating gray matter atrophy to speech fluency in FTLD subgroups. The cohort includes a social/executive (SOC/EXEC) subgroup characterized by social comportment and executive deficits consistent with behavioral-variant FTD. Imaging was performed on a subset (n=22 patients; SOC/EXEC n=9) and contrasted against age-matched controls (n=31) using whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses in MNI space; subgroup-specific atrophy maps and overlaps with fluency-related voxels are reported in figures and tables. Sample sizes meet the >=6 patient and >=6 control thresholds for the SOC/EXEC imaging subgroup. Thus the study provides whole-brain, between-group VBM results for a bvFTD-like group. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analysis, review article, disallowed modality) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, appendices).

This grant-report summarizes multiple studies but does not present a whole-brain voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) between-group contrast comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (or Pick’s disease) group to controls. Inclusion met: I3 (FDG-PET analyses are described). Inclusion not met: I4 (no explicit bvFTD patient group reported with details), I5 (no clear patient group sizes ≥6 for bvFTD), I6 (no between-group voxelwise coordinates for bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly from a bvFTD sample). Exclusion applied: E6 (reports mainly ROI/atlas-based, classification, and summary results without qualifying whole-brain voxelwise coordinates for bvFTD). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

execution_stats.search_query: (behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia OR bvFTD OR frontal variant frontotemporal dementia OR frontotemporal dementia OR picks disease) AND (functional magnetic resonance imaging OR fMRI OR voxel-based morphometry OR VBM OR positron emission tomography OR PET)
